p0.original: 关键问题：不同感觉有什么相同之处和不同之处
p0.en: Key issues: What are the similarities and differences between different perceptions?

p2.original: 不同感觉的工作方式基本相同，但每一种感觉会各自提取不同的信息，并将其发送到大脑中各自的专门加工区域。
p2.en: The working methods of different feelings are essentially the same, but each feeling extracts different information from each other and sends it to their respective specialized processing areas in the brain.

p3.original: 视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉、痛觉、本体觉：在某些方面，所有这些感觉都是相同的。我们已经知道它们都能将刺激能量转化为神经脉冲。它们对变化刺激比对恒定刺激更敏感。它们都为我们提供了关于世界的信息，这些信息具有生存价值。但是它们有什么不同呢？
p3.en: Visual, hearing, smell, taste, touch, pain, instinct: in some respects, all these feelings are the same. We already know that they can turn the stimulant energy into a nerve pulse. They are more sensitive to change incentives than to constant ones. They all provide us with information about the world, which is of life value. But what difference does it make?

p4.original: 除了痛觉，每种感觉都会产生不同形式的刺激能量，并将其提取的信息发送到大脑的不同部分。不同感觉的这些对比引导我们找到这一学习阶段的核心概念：
p4.en: Except for pain, each feeling produces different forms of irritation energy and sends the information it extracts to different parts of the brain. These contrasts of perception lead us to the core concept of this learning phase:

p5.original: 不同感觉的工作方式基本相同，但每一种感觉会各自提取不同的信息，并将其发送到大脑中各自的专门加工区域。
p5.en: The working methods of different feelings are essentially the same, but each feeling extracts different information from each other and sends it to their respective specialized processing areas in the brain.

p6.original: 这样的结果是，不同感觉的产生是因为大脑的不同区域接收了信息。你是听到钟声还是看到钟最终取决于大脑的哪个部分加工了输入。我们将通过依次观察每种感觉来探索这一切是如何运作的。首先，我们将聚焦于视觉系统，看看它是如何将光波转化为颜色和亮度的视觉感觉的。视觉是我们最了解的感觉。
p6.en: As a result, different feelings arise because different regions of the brain receive information. Do you hear the bells or do you see the bells eventually depend on which part of the brain is processed for input? We will explore how this works by looking at each feeling in turn. First of all, we will focus on the visual system, and see how it translates light waves into a sense of colour and brightness. Visuality is the feeling we know most.

p14.original: 解释视觉系统如何对光进行加工，并形成视觉感受。
p14.en: Explain how the visual system processes light and creates visual perception.

p15.original: 拥有良好视力的动物具有巨大的生物学优势。这一事实成为进化的动力，使视觉成为人类和大多数其他频繁活动的生物最复杂、最发达、最重要的感觉。良好的视觉帮助我们发现所期望的目标、威胁和物理环境的变化，并有助于我们对行为做出相应调整。那么，视觉系统是如何做到这一点的呢？
p15.en: Animals with good vision have great biological advantages. This fact has become the driving force of evolution, making vision the most complex, developed and most important feeling of life in humans and most other frequent activities. Good vision helps us to detect desired goals, threats and changes in the physical environment, and helps us to adapt our behaviour accordingly. So, how does the visual system do that?

p16.original: 3.4.1 视觉解剖：神经系统如何对光进行加工
p16.en: 3.4.1 Visual anatomy: how the neurological system processes light

p17.original: 你可能认为眼睛类似于“摄像机”，大脑用它来拍摄世界的动态图像（见图3-3）。
p17.en: You may think the eyes are similar to the “cybers”, which are used by the brain to take dynamic images of the world (see figures 3-3).

p19.original: 就像照相机一样，眼睛通过晶状体聚集光线，将其聚焦，然后在眼睛后部的视网膜（retina）上形成图像。顺便说一下，晶状体会将图像左右翻转且上下颠倒。（因为视觉非常重要，这种视觉翻转可能影响了大脑的结构，所以大脑的感觉加工区域往往保持了这种翻转。因此，大部分来自感觉器官的信息会传递到大脑的对侧。同样，身体在大脑感觉区的“地图”通常是翻转和颠倒的。）
p19.en: As with cameras, the eyes gather light through crystals, focus it and then create images on the retina in the back of the eye. By the way, the crystals turn the image around and upside down. (Because of the importance of vision, which may affect the structure of the brain, the sense processing area of the brain tends to maintain this reversal. Thus, most of the information from the sensory organs is transmitted to the opposite side of the brain. Similarly, the “map” of the body in the brain area is usually reversed and reversed. I don't think so.

p20.original: 但是，数码相机只是简单地形成一个电子图像，而眼睛形成的图像会在大脑中得到进一步的加工。眼睛的独有性使眼睛不同于其他感觉器官的地方在于它能从光波中提取信息（光波是一种电磁能量）。然后，眼睛将光的特性转化为大脑可以加工的神经信号。这种信号转导发生在视网膜上，视网膜是眼睛后部的感光细胞层，其作用很像数码相机中的感光芯片。
p20.en: However, digital cameras simply form an electronic image, while eye-forming images are further processed in the brain. The uniqueness of the eyes makes them different from other sensory organs in that they extract information from the light waves (which are an electromagnetic energy). The eyes then turn the characteristic of light into a neurotonic signal that the brain can process. This signal transfer takes place on the retina, which is the sensory cell layer in the back of the eye, acting much like a sensory chip in a digital camera.

p21.original: 而且，和照相机一样，眼睛也会出错。例如，“近视”者的晶状体把图像聚焦在视网膜的前方；而“远视”者的焦点延伸到视网膜的后面。如果没有矫正镜片，两种情况下的图像都不清晰。
p21.en: And, like the camera, there's a mistake in the eye. For example, the crystals of the "near vision" focus the image on the front of the retina; And the focus of the "discretion" extends to the back of the retina. Without orthotic lenses, the images are not clear in either case.

p22.original: 视网膜的真正工作由称为光感受器（photoreceptors）的感光细胞完成，其工作原理与数码相机中的微小像素感受器非常相似。这些光感受器由两种不同类型的特殊神经元组成，即视杆细胞（rods）和视锥细胞（cones），它们吸收光能并通过产生神经信息做出反应（见图3-4）。但是为什么有两种感光细胞呢？
p22.en: The true work of the retina is done by the photons called photons (photoreceptors), which work in very similar ways to micro-pixel sensors in digital cameras. These photoreceptors consist of two distinct types of neurons, namely, rods and cones, which absorb light energy and react by producing neuro-information (see figure 3-4). But why are there two sensory cells?

p23.original: 图3-4 视网膜上光的转导
p23.en: Figure 3-4: Transfer of light on the retina

p24.original: 因为我们有时在接近黑暗的环境下工作，有时在明亮的光线下工作，所以我们进化出两种处理器类型——两种以形状命名的不同的感受器细胞类型。有1.25亿个微小的视杆细胞，它们负责“暗视觉”，即它们能在夜间探测到低强度的光，但它们无法做出细微的区别，所以无法引起我们对颜色的感觉。视杆细胞能让你在黑暗的电影院里找到座位。
p24.en: Because we sometimes work near darkness, sometimes under bright light, we evolve two types of processor -- two different sensor cell types named in shape. There are 125 million tiny sight rod cells that are responsible for “dark vision”, i.e. they detect low-intensity light at night, but they can't make a fine difference, so they can't give us a sense of color. The sight rod cells can get you a seat in a dark cinema.

p25.original: 在更明亮的光线下，700万个视锥细胞的工作就是对色觉进行必要的精细区分。视锥细胞专门用来探测我们感觉到的蓝色、红色或绿色光波。在良好的光线下，我们可以用这些视锥细胞来区分成熟的西红柿（感觉为红色）和未成熟的西红柿（感觉为绿色）。视锥细胞集中在视网膜中心一个叫作中央凹（fovea）的小区域，该区域赋予了我们最敏锐的视觉。随着眼球的运动，我们用中央凹来扫描我们视觉上感兴趣的任何东西，例如，一张面孔或者一朵花的特征。
p25.en: In brighter light, 7 million cone cells work to make the necessary fine distinction between colours. The cone cells are designed to detect the blue, red or green light waves we feel. In good light, we can use these cone cells to distinguish between mature tomatoes (which feel red) and premature tomatoes (which feel green). The cone cells are concentrated in a small area at the centre of the retina called Fovea, which gives us the sharpest vision. With eyeballs, we scan anything that is visually interesting, for example, a face or a flower.

p26.original: 视网膜也含有对物体边缘和边界敏感的感受器细胞；其他细胞对光、影和运动做出反应（Werblin & Roska，2007）。然而，视网膜中还有两种重要的细胞对光没有直接反应。最近发现的米勒细胞（Müllercells）是一种漏斗状的胶质细胞（glialcells），它将光线通过视网膜层传导到眼睛后部感光的视杆和视锥细胞（Franze et al.，2007）。需要注意的是，光到达光感受器后，它在视觉系统里的旅程就到此为止了。在那里，视杆和视锥将光转化为电化学信息，通过视神经传递到大脑。
p26.en: Retinal membranes also contain sensor cells sensitive to the edge and boundaries of objects; Other cells react to light, shadow and motion (Werblin & Roska, 2007). However, there are two other important cells in the retina that do not react directly to light. The recently discovered Millercells (Müllercells) are a funnel-like glidcells, which transmit light through retinas to sight poles and cone cells that sense light in the back of the eye (Franze et al., 2007). It is important to note that the journey to the light sensor ends when it arrives in the visual system. There, vision poles and cones transform light into electrochemical information and transmit it to the brain through the optic nerve.

p27.original: 把视觉信息传递给大脑
p27.en: Send visual information to the brain.

p28.original: 双极细胞（bipolar cells）从视网膜的数百万光感受器（视杆细胞和视锥细胞）收集信息，并将其传送给视网膜神经节细胞（retinal ganglion cells），就像航空枢纽从许多地区机场汇集乘客并将其运送到其他目的地一样。神经节细胞的轴突捆绑在一起构成视神经（optic nerve），将视觉信息从眼睛传输到大脑（见图3-3和图3-4）。
p28.en: Bipolar cells collect information from millions of photo-receptors of the retina (revision poles and cone cells) and transmit it to retinatural neurological cells (retinatural gangliom cells), just as the aviation hub assembles passengers from many regional airports and transports them to other destinations. The axial bundling of neuronosyte forms the optic nerve (optic neve) and transmits visual information from the eyes to the brain (see figures 3-3 and 3-4).

p29.original: 奇怪的是，每只眼睛的视网膜上都有一小块区域，是每个人都有的盲区，因为那部分视网膜没有感光细胞。这个盲点（blind spot）位于每只眼睛的视神经出口处，结果在视野中形成一个小孔。你不会因为有盲点而失明，因为一只眼睛错过的东西会被另一只眼睛记录下来，大脑会用与背景匹配的信息“填补”这个点。你可以按照“试一试”栏目中的说明找到自己的盲点。
p29.en: Strangely, there is a small area on each eye's retina, which is a blind area for everyone, because that part of the retina has no light cells. This blind spot (blind spot) is located at the optic nerve exit of each eye, resulting in a small hole in the horizon. You're not blind because there's a blind spot, because something missing in one eye is recorded in the other eye, and the brain uses information that matches the background to "fill" the point. You can find your own blind spot, as indicated in the "Try" column.

p30.original: 应该澄清的是，我们称之为失明的视力障碍可能有许多原因，这些原因通常与盲点无关。例如，视网膜损伤、使晶状体不透明的白内障、视神经损伤或大脑视觉加工区域损伤都可能导致失明。
p30.en: It should be clarified that there may be many reasons for what we call blindness, which are usually not related to blind spots. For example, retina damage, cataracts that make crystals intransparent, optic neural damage or damage to areas of brain visual processing can lead to blindness.

p31.original: 除了盲点，我们在距离中央凹的手指宽度之外（Macknik & Martinez-Conde，2014）的区域内都是法律意义上的盲人（在20/200视力之下）。你现在可以通过以下方式来验证这一点：盯着这句话中的某个词，在眼睛不动的情况下试着去读两边一两个词之外的东西。如果你的视力很好，你可能就会觉得我们的整个视野都很清晰。但事实并非如此。这是你的大脑耍的把戏！你实际上是根据记忆填补了视野的模糊性，一部分是根据你认为应该在那里的东西来填补，一部分是根据场景的视觉模式来填充，就像你通过眼动扫描了一样。
p31.en: Apart from the blind spot, we are legally blind (under 20/200 eyesight) in the area of our finger width from the central dent (Macknik & Martinez-Conde, 2014). Now you can prove this by staring at a word in this sentence and trying to read something other than one or two words without moving your eyes. If your eyesight is good, you might think our whole vision is clear. But that is not the case. This is your brain trick! You actually filled the ambiguity of the vision with memory, partly with what you think should be there, and partly with the visual pattern of the scene, just like you scanned it by eye.

p32.original: 说到眼球运动，你的眼睛不断地在做微小的、不自主的运动，我们称之为微眼跳（microsaccades）（Martinez-Conde & Macknik，2011）。为了弄清这些微小运动对我们的影响，科学家们在20世纪50年代进行了一项实验，他们成功地将图像完全静止在视网膜上。（他们使用了隐形眼镜，并配上一个非常小的投影仪。）结果发现，以这种方式保持稳定的图像似乎时隐时现。最近的实验还表明，当观看某些视觉图像时，微眼跳会让我们在没有运动的时候感知到运动（见图3-5）。
p32.en: Speaking of eyeball sports, your eyes are constantly doing tiny, uninvolved sports, which we call microsaccades (Martinez-Conde & Macknik, 2011). In order to ascertain the impact of these micro-movements on us, scientists conducted an experiment in the 1950s that succeeded in placing images completely static on the retina. (They used contact lenses and had a very small projector. As a result, images that remain stable in this way appear to be present from time to time. Recent experiments have also shown that microeye leaps can give us a sense of motion when we see some visual images without moving (see figure 3-5).

p34.original: 注：这幅由伊西娅·莱万特（Isia Leviant）创作的艺术作品《谜》（The Enigma），展示了所谓的“微眼跳”（持续的微小眼球运动）是如何让我们在静止的图像中产生运动错觉的。静止图像中根本没有真正的运动。
p34.en: Note: This art by Isia Levant, The Enigma, shows how so-called “microeye leaps” (continuous little eye movement) can create motion illusions in static images. There is no real movement in the static images.

p35.original: 试一试 找到自己的盲点
p35.en: Try and find your own blind spot.

p36.original: “盲点”指视网膜上的某个地方，在该处视网膜上的神经元聚集在一起，从眼球中穿出来形成视神经。此处的视网膜上没有感光细胞。因此，你在视野的这个小区域是“盲”的。下面的演示将帮助你确定这个盲点在你的视野中出现的位置（见图3-6）。
p36.en: “Break spot” means a place on the retina where neurons gather together and come out of the eyeball to form the optic nerve. There's no light cells on the retina here. So, you're blind in this small area of vision. The following presentation will help you determine where this blind spot appears in your vision (see figures 3-6).

p39.original: 与图像保持一臂的距离（或者，如果你在大屏幕上观看的话，把你的眼睛移近一点）。然后闭上你的右眼，把左眼固定在“银行”的图形上。保持右眼闭上，慢慢靠近图像。当它在15～30厘米处（取决于屏幕上图像的大小），并且美元符号处于你的盲点上时，美元符号会消失，但你不会在视野中看到一个“洞”。相反，你的视觉系统会用背景中的信息来填充缺少的区域。你把钱“丢”了！
p39.en: Keep an arm away from the image (or, if you look on the big screen, close your eyes a little). And then close your right eye and stick your left eye on the bank. Keep your right eye closed and slowly approach the image. When it's 15-30 centimetres (depending on the size of the image on the screen) and the dollar symbol is on your blind spot, the dollar symbol will disappear, but you will not see a "hole" in your vision. Instead, your visual system fills the missing areas with information from the background. You lost the money!

p41.original: 大脑会用适当的背景填充视野中缺失的部分。为了让你自己相信这一点，再次闭上右眼，将注意力集中在图中十字架上（见图3-7）。再次，保持右眼闭上，当左眼将注意力集中在十字架上时，向图像靠近。这一次，线中的空隙将消失，并用两边的线的延续来填补。这表明你在盲点看到的东西可能并不存在！
p41.en: The brain fills missing parts of the field of view with appropriate background. In order to convince you of this, you will again close your right eye and focus on the cross in the picture (see figure 3-7). Once again, keep your right eye closed and approach the image as the left eye focuses its attention on the cross. This time, the gap in the line will disappear and be filled with the continuation of the line on both sides. Which means that what you see in the blind spot may not exist!

p43.original: 3.4.2 大脑中的视觉感觉加工
p43.en: 3.4.2 Visual perception processing in the brain

p44.original: 我们用眼睛看，但看见东西的是大脑。换句话说，一个叫作视觉皮层（visual cortex）的特殊大脑区域通过视神经从眼睛输入的信息产生视觉图像（见图3-8）。正如我们所看到的（可以这么说），视野中物体发出的光将图像投射到眼睛的视网膜上。现在请注意两件重要的事情：第一，眼睛的晶状体反转了视网膜上的图像，所以左边的所有东西都落在视网膜的右边，右边的所有东西则都落在了视网膜的左边（图3-8将帮助你直观地看到这一点）；第二，视觉系统分离来自每只眼睛的视网膜图像，使来自每只眼睛的部分图像传到大脑的另一侧（注意视觉通路的分支如何在视交叉处交叉）。
p44.en: We look with our eyes, but it's the brain that sees things. In other words, a special brain area called visual cortex produces visual images of the information entered from the eye through the visual nerve (see figures 3-8). As we can see (in this case), the light from the object in the horizon projectes the image into the retina of the eye. Now, attention is drawn to two important things: first, the crystal of the eyes reverses the image on the retina, so everything on the left side falls on the right side of the retina, and everything on the right side falls on the left side of the retina (figures 3-8 will help you visualize this); Second, the visual system separates retinal images from each eye, allowing some images from each eye to reach the other side of the brain (see how the branches of the visual circuit are crossed at the intersection of the vision).

p45.original: 因此，出现在双眼视野左侧的物体（图3-8中的男子）被发送到右半球的视皮层进行加工，而双眼视野右侧的物体（图3-8中的妇女）被发送到左视皮层。一般来说，右半球“看到”左视野，而左半球“看到”右视野。
p45.en: Thus, objects appearing on the left side of the two-eye horizon (the men in figure 3-8) are sent to the skin layer in the right hemisphere for processing, while objects on the right side of the two-eye horizon (the women in figure 3-8) are sent to the left-eye layer. In general, the right hemisphere “sees” the left horizon, while the left hemisphere “sees” the right horizon.

p46.original: 图3-8 视觉刺激是如何从眼睛传到大脑的
p46.en: Figure 3-8: How visual irritation is transmitted from the eyes to the brain

p47.original: 注：大脑中的视野是反转的，因为晶状体会反转视网膜上的图像（此外，视觉通路的构造使右视皮层“看到”左视野，左视皮层“看到”右视野）。（Frisby，1980）
p47.en: Note: The vision in the brain is inverted because the crystals reverse the image on the membrane (in addition, the construction of the visual circuit allows the right optic cortex to “see” the left optic cortex to “see” the right rim. (Frisby, 1980)

p48.original: 在视觉皮层，大脑开始发挥它的魔力，将传入的神经信息转化为颜色、形状、边界和运动的视觉感觉。令人惊讶的是，视觉皮层也设法根据两只眼睛提取的二维图案建立我们的三维深度世界（Barinaga，1998；Dobbins et al.，1998）。经过进一步的加工，大脑皮层最终将这些视觉感受与记忆、动机、情绪以及身体位置和触觉的感觉结合起来，从而创造出符合我们当前关注和感兴趣的视觉世界的表征（de Gelder，2000；Vuilleumier & Huang，2009）。这些联系解释了为什么当你去超市购物时，如果你饥肠辘辘，你就会强烈地被开胃食品所吸引。
p48.en: In the visual cortex, the brain begins to exercise its magic by transforming the incoming neural information into the visual feeling of colour, shape, boundary and movement. Surprisingly, the visual cortex has also managed to build our three-dimensional depth world based on a two-dimensional pattern extracted from two eyes (Barinaga, 1998); Dobbins et al., 1998). After further processing, the cortex of the brain eventually combines these visions with memories, motivations, emotions, and the physical position and touch, thus creating signs of a visual world that meet our current concerns and interests (de Gelder, 2000); Vuilleumier & Huang, 2009. These connections explain why when you go shopping at the supermarket, if you get hungry, you're attracted to appetizers.

p49.original: 让我们回到本章的思考题，“我们所看到的世界是否和其他人一样？”就感觉而言，我们发现答案应该是“是”。也就是说，不同的人基本上有相同的感觉器官（除了少数人，如乔纳森等不能分辨颜色或有其他感觉缺陷的人）。因此，我们可以合理地假设，大多数人对颜色、声音、质地、气味和味道的感觉方式大致相同，不过我们将看到，他们知觉的方式并不一定相同。为了理解其中的意思，让我们从亮度的视觉感觉开始。
p49.en: Let us return to the subject of this chapter, “Do we see a world like others? “In sense, we find that the answer should be yes. In other words, different people have essentially the same sensory organs (except for a few people who cannot distinguish between colours or other sensory defects, such as Jonathan). Thus, we can reasonably assume that most people feel the same colour, sound, texture, smell and taste, but we will see that they do not necessarily feel the same way. In order to understand what it means, let's start with the visual sense of brightness.

p50.original: 视觉系统如何产生亮度
p50.en: How does the visual system produce brightness?

p51.original: 亮度（brightness）的感觉来自光的强度或振幅，取决于到达视网膜的光的强弱（见表3-2）。
p51.en: The feeling of brightness comes from the strength or amplitude of the light, depending on the strength and weakness of the light reaching the retina (see tables 3-2).

p52.original: 表3-2 视觉刺激变成感觉
p52.en: Table 3-2 Visual irritation becomes a feeling

p53.original: 注：颜色和亮度是光波波长和强度的心理对应物。波长和强度是光波的物理特征，而颜色和亮度是只存在于大脑中的心理特征。
p53.en: Note: Colours and brightness are psychological counterparts for the wavelength and intensity of light. Wavelength and intensity are physical features of light waves, while colour and brightness are psychological characteristics that exist only in the brain.

p54.original: 来自太阳的强光会产生更强烈的光波，从而在视网膜中产生更多的神经活动，而来自月球的相对较暗的光则会产生相对较少的视网膜活动。最终，大脑通过从眼睛接收到的神经活动量来感觉亮度。
p54.en: Strong light from the Sun produces greater light waves, resulting in more neuroactivity in the retina, while relatively dark light from the Moon produces relatively few retina activity. Ultimately, the brain senses brightness through the amount of neuroactivity received from the eyes.

p55.original: 视觉系统如何产生色彩
p55.en: How the visual system is colored.

p56.original: 你可能已经惊讶地发现花或成熟的西红柿本身没有颜色（color）或色调（hue）。矛盾的是，在明亮的光线下看到的物体似乎有一种神奇的特性，那就是充满了色彩；但正如我们所注意到的，红色的西红柿、黄色的花、绿色的树、蓝色的海洋和多色的彩虹实际上是无色的。我们感觉它们有不同的颜色，其实是因为它们反射不同波长的光，但光本身没有颜色，只有波长。尽管世界在我们看来是这样，但是颜色在大脑之外并不存在，因为颜色是大脑根据进入我们眼睛的光的波长产生的感觉。因此，色彩只存在于观察者的头脑之中——这是我们感觉体验的心理特性。为了更全面地理解这是如何发生的，你必须先了解光的本质。
p56.en: You may have been surprised to discover that the flowers or mature tomatoes themselves do not have color (color) or hue. Paradoxically, objects seen in bright light seem to have a magical characteristic, which is colourful; But, as we have noticed, red tomatoes, yellow flowers, green trees, blue oceans and coloured rainbows are actually colorless. We feel they have different colours, actually because they reflect light with different wavelengths, but the light itself has no color, only wavelengths. Although the world looks like this to us, colour does not exist outside the brain, because it is the feeling of the brain based on the wavelength of the light that enters our eyes. Therefore, colour exists only in the minds of observers — the psychological characteristics that we feel to experience. In order to understand more fully how this happened, you must first understand the nature of light.

p57.original: 眼睛只能探测到我们称之为可见光的一小部分能量。物理学家告诉我们，这种光与无线电波、微波、红外光、紫外线、X射线和宇宙射线基本相同。所有这些都是电磁能的某种形式。当这些波在空间中振动时，它们的波长不同（它们在一个波周期中传播的距离），就像池塘上的涟漪（见图3-9）。我们看到的光只占据了巨大电磁波谱（electro-magnetic spectrum）中央附近的一小部分。我们只有通过一个叫作可见光谱（visible spectrum）的小视窗才能直接接触到这个电磁波谱。因为我们没有对电磁波谱的其他部分敏感的生物感受器，所以我们必须通过无线电和电视等设备来探测这些波，这些设备将能量转换成我们可以感觉的信号。
p57.en: The eye can only detect a fraction of what we call visible light. Physics tells us that this light is basically the same as radio waves, microwaves, infrared light, ultraviolet light, X-rays and cosmic rays. All these are some kind of electromagnetic energy. When these waves vibrate in space, they vary in wavelengths (the distance from which they spread in a wave cycle), as in the case of the ponds (see figures 3-9). The light that we see is only a small fraction of the center of the huge electromagnetic spectrum. We can only get direct access to this electromagnetic spectrum through a small window called Visible Spectrum. Because we don't have bioreceptors that are sensitive to other parts of the electromagnetic spectrum, we have to detect those waves through equipment like radio and television, which converts energy into a signal that we can feel.

p58.original: 在狭窄的可见光谱中，不同波长的光波使我们产生不同颜色的感觉。西红柿反射的较长的光波使我们看到红色，中等长度的光波使我们看到柠檬和酸橙的黄色和绿色。晴空中的短波刺激出蓝色的感觉。眼睛从光的波长中提取信息，大脑利用这些信息构建出我们看见的颜色的感觉（见表3-2）。
p58.en: In the narrow visible spectrum, different wavelengths of light give us different colours. Long light waves reflecting tomatoes make us see red, medium length light waves make us see lemon and orange yellow and green. Short waves in the clear sky stimulate the blue feeling. The eye extracts information from the wavelength of the light, and the brain uses it to construct the feeling of the colour we see (see tables 3-2).

p59.original: 值得注意的是，我们对颜色、形状、位置和深度的视觉体验的基础是大脑皮层的不同区域对视觉感觉信息流的加工。大脑在一个特殊的区域进行颜色加工，人类能够区分大约500万种不同的颜色。正是大脑皮层这一部分的损伤使乔纳森看不见颜色。附近的其他皮层区域则负责加工有关边界、形状和运动的信息。
p59.en: It is noteworthy that our visual experience of colour, shape, location and depth is based on the processing of visual sensory information streams in different areas of the cortex of the brain. The brain processes colours in a particular area, and humans can distinguish about 5 million different colours. It's the part of the cortex that makes Jonathan invisible. Other areas of the cortex in the vicinity are responsible for processing information on boundaries, shapes and movements.

p61.original: 注：可见光和其他形式的电磁波之间的唯一区别是波长。我们眼睛中的感受器只对电磁波谱的一小部分敏感（Sekuler & Blake，1994）。
p61.en: Note: The only difference between visible light and other forms of electromagnetic waves is wavelength. The sensor in our eyes is sensitive to only a small fraction of the electromagnetic spectrum (Sekuler & Blake, 1994).

p63.original: 尽管颜色是在大脑皮层中实现的，颜色加工却是从视网膜开始。在那里，三种不同类型的视锥细胞感觉可见光谱光波的不同部分，即我们感觉到红色、绿色和蓝色的光波。这种根据三类光感受器对色觉进行解释的理论被称为三原色理论（trichromatic theory），有一段时间它被认为可以完全解释色觉。我们现在知道，三原色理论能最好地解释视锥细胞的色觉的初始阶段。
p63.en: Although colours are realized in the cortex of the brain, the colour process begins with the retina. There, three different types of cone cells feel visible in different parts of the spectrum, that is, we feel red, green and blue. This theory of interpretation of colour based on three types of light sensor is known as trichromical theory, which for some time was considered to be fully capable of interpreting colour. We now know that the three-protocol theory best explains the initial phase of the chromosomal perception of cone cells.

p64.original: 另一种解释，被称为拮抗加工理论（opponent-process theory），它可以更好地解释负后像（afterimage）（见“试一试”版块），负后像是一种涉及拮抗或互补颜色的现象。根据拮抗加工理论，视觉系统从双极细胞开始，就以互补成对的方式（红-绿或黄-蓝）加工颜色。因此，某种颜色（如红色）的感觉会抑制或干扰其补色（绿色）的感觉。综上所述，这两种理论解释了涉及视网膜和视觉通路的色觉的两个不同方面。虽然这听起来很复杂，但这里重要的信息是：
p64.en: Another explanation, called the Opponent-process theory, can better explain negative hindsight (see “test-out” section), which is a phenomenon involving resistance or complementary colours. According to the theory of stress processing, the visual system begins with a bipolar cell and processes colours in a mutually reinforcing manner (red-green or yellow-blue). Thus, a feeling of a colour (e.g. red) inhibits or interferes with the feeling of its complementary (green) colour. In summary, the two theories explain two different aspects of colour that involve retinas and visual access. Although it sounds complicated, the important message here is:

p65.original: 三原色理论解释了视网膜视锥细胞的颜色加工过程，而拮抗加工理论解释了双极细胞和其他细胞的颜色加工过程。
p65.en: The triochromic theory explains the colour process of retina cone cells, while the resistance theory explains the colour process of bipolar and other cells.

p67.original: 不过，并不是每个人看见的颜色都一样。有些人天生就缺乏辨别颜色的能力，这通常是由于视网膜上感应颜色的视锥细胞的遗传缺陷造成的（但是，请注意，乔纳森的色盲是由于大脑中的颜色加工区域受损造成的）。色盲发病率因种族而异（白人最高，黑人最低）。总体来说，美国大约有8%的男性受色盲影响，女性中则很少有色盲。
p67.en: But not everyone sees the same color. Some people are born to lack the ability to identify colours, usually due to genetic defects in the optical cone cells with the colours felt on the retina (but note that Jonathan's color blindness is due to damage to the colour processing area in the brain). The incidence of colour blindness varies according to race (whites are the highest and blacks the lowest). Overall, about 8 per cent of men in the United States are affected by colour blindness, while very few are women.

p68.original: 在极端情况下会出现全色盲（color blindness），即彻底不能辨别颜色。常见的情况则是，人们只是在某种颜色上有色弱，导致识别颜色时存在小小的问题（特别是在弱光条件下）。有一种色弱的人不能分辨淡色，如粉红色或棕黄色。然而，大多数色弱或色盲是在区分红色和绿色时有问题，尤其是在弱饱和度时。那些混淆黄色和蓝色的人很少见，大约每千人中只有一到两个人。最罕见的是那些根本看不到颜色却只能看到亮度变化的人。事实上，只有大约500例这种完全色盲的病例被报道过，包括我们在本章开头介绍过的乔纳森。要检查你是否有色觉缺陷，请看图3-10。如果你在图案中看出数字29，你的色觉可能就是正常的。如果你看到别的东西，你可能就有色弱或色盲。
p68.en: In extreme cases, there is full colour blindness, i.e. completely undiscoverable colour. It is common for people to have weak colours in a certain colour, leading to minor problems in identifying colours (especially in light conditions). There is a person of weak colour who cannot distinguish light, such as pink or brown. However, most colourless or colour-blind are problematic when distinguishing between red and green, especially when it comes to saturation. Those who confuse yellow and blue are rare, with only one or two people per 1,000. The rarest are those who can't see color at all but see brightness change. In fact, only about 500 cases of this total colour blindness have been reported, including Jonathan, which we described at the beginning of this chapter. To check if you have color defects, see figures 3-10. If you can see the number 29 in the chart, your color may be normal. If you see something else, you may have a weak color or a color blind.

p69.original: 任何两种原色光的组合产生第三种原色光的补色光。所有三种波长的组合产生白光（印刷用的颜料的混合的原理与此不同，颜料会吸收落在它们上面的某些波长的光）。
p69.en: The combination of any two types of original light produces the supplementary light of the third. All three wavelength combinations produce white light (the mix of pigments for printing is different, and paints absorb some wavelength light that falls above them).

p71.original: 注：不能区分红色和绿色的人将无法识别隐藏在图形中的数字。你看到了什么？如果你在图案中看到数字29，你的色觉很可能就是正常的。
p71.en: Note: People who cannot distinguish between red and green will not be able to identify numbers hidden in graphics. What do you see? If you see the number 29 in the drawing, your color is probably normal.

p72.original: 试一试 令人惊奇的后像

p73.original: 当你盯着一个有颜色的物体一段时间后，你的视网膜上的神经节细胞就会变得疲劳，从而产生一种有趣的视觉效果。当你把视线移到一个空白的白色表面时，你可以看到一个互补色的物体，这就是视觉后像。“补色旗”演示将向你展示它是如何发生的。盯着绿色、黑色和橙色旗帜中心的圆点至少30秒。注意保持眼睛稳定，不要让他们在这段时间扫描图像。然后迅速将目光转移到一张白纸的中心或一堵浅色的空白墙上。你看到了什么？可以让你的朋友们也试试。他们能看到相同的后像吗？（对于色盲的人来说，效果可能不一样。）
p73.en: When you look at a colored object for some time, the neuronocells on your retina get tired, and have an interesting visual effect. When you move your sight to a blank white surface, you can see a complementary object, and that's the visual image. The "Small Flag" demonstration will show you how it happened. The dots that stare at the centre of the green, black and orange flags will be at least 30 seconds. Keep your eyes steady and don't let them scan the images during this time. The eyes were then quickly transferred to the centre of a white paper or to a light blank wall. What do you see? It'll give your friends a chance. Can they see the same shadow? (For color-blind people, the effects may be different. I don't think so.

p74.original: 后像可以是负的，也可以是正的。正后像是由受到刺激后的感受器和神经过程的延续引起的。正后像很短暂。例如，当你在7月4日看到狂欢者旋转的闪烁烟花棒的轨迹时，可能就会产生正后像。负后像与最初的体验相反，如下面的“补色旗”（见图3-11）。负后像的持续时间更长。根据颜色视觉的拮抗加工理论，负后像的产生涉及视网膜和视神经的神经节细胞。当暴露在白光之下时，这些疲劳的细胞就产生了负后像中补色的感觉。
p74.en: It can be negative, it can be positive. It's like it's caused by the continuation of the irritator and the nervous process. Right after it looks like it's short. For example, when you see the trajectories of the sparkling fireworks rods of the carnival on 4 July, you may have a positive image. The negative backslides, contrary to the initial experience, are the following “subsidiary flags” (see figure 3-11). Negative after-like longer duration. According to the theory of colour visual resistance, negative hierarchies are produced in retinas and neurological neurological cells. When exposed to white light, these tired cells have the feeling of negative rearmament.

p78.original: 解释听觉系统是如何产生声音的。
p78.en: Explain how the hearing system produces sound.

p79.original: 想象一下，如果你的听力突然减弱，你的世界会发生怎样的变化。你很快就会发现，听觉和视觉一样，能让你定位空间中的物体，例如，一个叫你名字的声音的来源。事实上，在将我们引向远处的事件时，听觉可能比视觉更重要。在我们看到声音的来源之前，我们常常先听到声音，如身后传来的脚步声。听觉也可以告诉我们一些我们看不见的事件，包括语音、音乐或一辆驶来的汽车。
p79.en: Imagine how your world will change if your hearing suddenly weakens. You'll soon find that the hearing and the vision allow you to locate objects in space, for example, the source of a voice calling your name. In fact, hearing may be more important than vision in the event that leads us far away. Before we see the source of the sound, we often hear the sound, like the footsteps coming from behind. We can also be told of some things we cannot see, including voice, music or a moving car.

p80.original: 然而，听觉不仅仅局限于它的功能。因此，我们应当更深入地了解我们是如何听到的。在接下来的部分，我们将回顾感觉心理学家们发现的关于声波是如何产生的，它们是如何被感觉的，以及这些声音的感觉是如何被解释的。
p80.en: However, hearing is not limited to its function. We should therefore have a deeper understanding of how we heard it. In the next part, we will look back at how the sound waves are produced, how they are felt, and how they are explained.

p81.original: 3.5.1 声音的物理学：声波是如何产生的
p81.en: 3.5.1 Physics of sound: how sound waves are generated

p82.original: 如果好莱坞电影播放一艘宇宙飞船或一颗行星爆炸的真实录像，那么应该完全没有声音！在太空中，没有空气或其他介质来传递声波，所以，若你是一颗恒星爆炸的目击者，你会经历令人毛骨悚然的沉默。在地球上，爆竹等爆炸物体的能量通常以声波的形式传递到周围的空气中。从本质上讲，快速振动的物体，如吉他弦、铃铛和声带，也会因为振动而来回推动空气分子。由此产生的压力变化以声波的形式向外传播，声波每秒可以传播344米。
p82.en: If a Hollywood movie shows a real video of a spacecraft or a planet explosion, there should be no sound at all! There is no air or other medium in space to transmit sound waves, so if you were a witness to a star explosion, you would experience a creepy silence. On Earth, the energy of explosives such as fireworks is usually transmitted to the surrounding air in the form of acoustic waves. In essence, rapidly vibrating objects, such as guitar strings, bells and acoustic cords, can also drive back and forth to air molecules as a result of vibration. The resulting pressure changes are transmitted outward in the form of acoustic waves, which can spread 344 metres per second.

p83.original: 音叉可以发出最纯的音调（见图3-12）。当用木槌敲击音叉时，音叉产生的声波非常干净，只有频率（frequency）和振幅（amplitude）两个特性。任何声波都有这两个物理特性，它们决定了声波如何被大脑感知。
p83.en: Sound fork can make the purest tunes (see figures 3-12). When the acoustic fork is struck with a wooden hammer, the soundwaves produced by the acoustic fork are very clean, except for the characteristics of frequency (frequency) and amplitude (amplitude). Any sound wave has these two physical properties that determine how the sound wave is felt by the brain.

p85.original: 注：音叉振动产生的声波会产生压缩和膨胀的空气波。
p85.en: Note: Acoustic waves generated by acoustic fork vibrations generate compressed and swelling air waves.

p86.original: 频率指的是波在给定时间内完成的振动或循环次数，这反过来又决定了声音的高低（音高/pitch）。频率通常以周期/秒（cps）或赫兹（Hz）表示。振幅表示声波的物理强度；它以声压或能量为单位来定义。当你调低音乐系统的音量时，你就是在降低扬声器或耳塞发出的声波的振幅。
p86.en: Frequency refers to the number of vibrations or cycles completed by wave within a given time, which in turn determines the high-altitude of the sound (sonic/pitch). Frequency is usually expressed as cycle/sec (cps) or Herz (Hz). amplitudes are the physical strength of acoustic waves; It is defined in the form of sound pressure or energy. When you lower the volume of the music system, you lower the amplitude of sound waves from loudspeakers or earplugs.

p87.original: 3.5.2 感觉声音：我们如何听到声波
p87.en: 3.5.2 Sound: How do we hear sound waves

p88.original: 就像视觉一样，声音的心理感觉需要将声波转导为神经脉冲并发送到大脑。这分为以下四个步骤。
p88.en: Like vision, the sound psychological feeling needs to be transposed to a nerve pulse and sent to the brain. This is divided into the following four steps.

p89.original: 1. 空气传播的声波被传送到内耳。在这个最初的转变过程中，空气的振动波进入外耳（也称为耳郭）并通过耳道进入鼓膜（tympanic membrane）（见图3-13）。这张绷得很紧的片状组织将振动传递到中耳的三块以它们的形状命名的听小骨：锤骨、砧骨、镫骨。这些骨骼将振动传递给位于内耳的主要听觉器官——耳蜗（cochlea）。
p89.en: 1. Air-borne sound waves are transmitted to inner ears. During this initial transition, the vibration waves of the air enter the outer ear (also known as Quo) and through the tympanic membrane (see figures 3-13). This tight-tweaked tissue conveys vibrations to three small listening bones named after them in their shapes: hammer bones, gill bones, gill bones. These bones convey vibrations to the main hearing organ in the inner ear, the cochlea.

p90.original: 2. 耳蜗将振动集中在基底膜上。在耳蜗中，原来空气传播的声波变成“水上传播”，因为耳蜗的螺旋管充满了液体。当镫骨在耳蜗底部的卵圆窗（oval window）口上振动时，振动使液体产生波动，就像潜艇在水中发出声呐进行探测一样。当流体波通过耳蜗传播时，它会引起基底膜（basilar membrance）的振动，基底膜是一条细细的穿过耳蜗的毛茸茸的组织。
p90.en: 2. The earring concentrates the vibration on the base membrane. In the snails, the sound waves of the air were transformed into “water-borne transmission”, because the snails were full of liquids. When the gills vibrate on the mouth of the oval window at the bottom of the snail, vibrations cause fluid to fluctuate, as if the submarines were sounding in the water for detection. When fluent waves are transmitted through the snail, they cause vibrations of the base membrance, which is a fine, hairy tissue that passes through the snail.

p91.original: 3. 基底膜将振动转为神经信息。振动的基底膜上的微小毛细胞的摆动会刺激与毛细胞相连的感觉神经末梢。然后，兴奋的神经元将基底膜的机械振动转为神经活动。
p91.en: 3. The base membrane converts vibration to neuroinformation. The movement of tiny hair cells on the vibrating substrate stimulates the sensory nerve endings associated with the hair cells. Then the excited neurons convert the mechanical vibration of the substrate to neuroactivity.

p92.original: 4. 神经信息被传递到大脑的听觉皮层。神经信号通过一束称为听神经的神经元离开耳蜗。两只耳朵的听神经在脑干相遇，脑干将听觉信息传递给大脑两侧。最终，信号会到达大脑颞叶的听觉皮层，并且被进行更高级的加工。
p92.en: 4. Neural information is transmitted to the hearing cortex of the brain. The nerve signals leave the snails through a bunch of neurons called hearing nerves. The hearing nerves of both ears meet at the brain stem, which transmits the hearing message to both sides of the brain. Ultimately, the signal reaches the hearing cortex of the brain leaves and is processed at a higher level.

p94.original: 注：耳部传导的声波振动鼓膜，鼓膜将振动传递给中耳的锤骨、砧骨、镫骨，并传递给卵圆窗和耳蜗中的液体。在那里，基底膜上的毛细胞通过向大脑发送听觉信息做出反应。
p94.en: Note: Acoustic vibrating drum membranes, which transmit vibrations to the hammer bones, gill bones, gill bones, and to liquids in egg vertebras and snails. There, the hair cells on the substrate react by sending a hearing message to the brain.

p95.original: 如果你觉得听觉系统很复杂，你可以把它看作是一个感觉“接力队”。声波先由外耳传入，然后从耳膜传递到中耳的听小骨。之后，这些骨骼将机械振动传递到内耳的耳蜗和基底膜，在那里它们最终转变成为神经信号，这些信号又被传递到大脑。这一系列的步骤将普通的振动转化为像音乐、门铃、耳语、喊叫和心理学讲座那样精彩纷呈的体验。
p95.en: If you think the hearing system is complicated, you can think of it as a sensor team. The sound waves are first passed in from the outside ear and then passed from the eardrum to the hearing bone in the middle ear. The bones then pass the mechanical vibrations to the inner ear snails and the substrates, where they eventually turn into nerve signals, which are then transmitted to the brain. This series of steps translates ordinary vibrations into wonderful experiences like music, doorbells, whispers, shouts and psychological lectures.

p96.original: 3.5.3 声音的心理特性：我们如何识别音高、响度和音色
p96.en: 3.5.3 Psychological characteristics of sound: how we recognize sound height, soundness and sound color

p97.original: 不管它们来自哪里，像光波一样的声波只有两个物理特性：频率和振幅。在下面的部分，我们将向你展示大脑如何将这两个特征转化为三种心理感受：音高、响度和音色。
p97.en: Wherever they come from, acoustics like light waves have only two physical properties: frequency and amplitude. In the following part, we'll show you how the brain transforms these two features into three psychological feelings: high sound, acousticity and sound.

p99.original: 声波的频率决定了声音的高低——一种被称为音高（pitch）的特性。高频产生高音，低频产生低音，如表3-3所示。和光一样，我们对声音的敏感度只涵盖自然界中声波的有限范围。人类听觉灵敏度的范围从低约20赫兹（良好音响系统中超低音扬声器的最低范围）到高达20000赫兹（由高质量音频系统中的高频高音扬声器产生）的频率。其他生物可以听到更高（狗）和更低（大象）的声音。
p99.en: The frequency of sound waves determines the high-lowness of the sound - a characteristic known as pitch. High frequency (HF) produces high sound, low frequency produces low noise, as shown in Table 3-3. Like light, our sensitivity to sound covers only a limited range of sound waves in nature. The human acoustic sensitivity ranges from about 20 Hz low (the minimum range of ultra-low speakers in a good sound system) to up to 20,000 Hz high-frequency loudspeakers in a high-quality audio system. Other organisms can hear higher (dogs) and lower (eye elephants).

p100.original: 表3-3 听觉刺激变成感觉

p101.original: 注：音高和响度是频率和振幅（声波的物理特征）的心理等价物。音高和响度的感觉只存在于大脑中。声波也可以是简单波的复杂组合。我们将这种复杂性称为音色。
p101.en: Note: Sound heights and acoustics are psychological equivalents of frequencies and amplitudes (physical characteristics of sound waves). The feeling of high sound and soundness is only in the brain. Acoustic waves can also be a complex combination of simple waves. We call this complexity the sound.

p102.original: 听觉器官如何产生音高的感觉？
p102.en: How do hearing organs feel high?

p103.original: 两个不同的听觉加工过程共同承担这项任务，它们一起提供的感觉精确度比单独任何一种加工能提供的都要高。下面是具体的加工过程。
p103.en: This task is shared by two different hearing processes, which together provide greater sense accuracy than can be provided by any single process. The following are specific processes.

p104.original: 声波通过内耳时，基底膜就会振动（见图3-12）。不同的频率激活膜上的不同位置。因此，人们听到的音高在一定程度上取决于基底膜的哪个区域受到了最大的刺激。位置理论对音高知觉的解释是，基底膜上的不同位置向大脑的听觉皮层发送不同音高的神经代码，就像钢琴键盘上不同位置的键可以发出不同的音符一样。位置理论解释了我们能听到高音（高于1000赫兹，即1000周期/秒）的能力。
p104.en: When acoustic waves pass through the inner ear, the substrate is vibrated (see figures 3-12). Different frequency activates different positions on the membrane. Thus, the sound is heard to a certain extent depending on which area of the base membrane has been the most stimulating. The position theory interprets the acoustic perception by sending different acoustic neurocodes to the acoustic cortex of the brain at different locations on the base membrane, just as the keys to the piano keyboard can send different notes. The location theory explains our ability to hear high voices (above 1,000 Hz, or 1,000 cycles/sec).

p105.original: 基底膜上的神经元以不同的频率对不同的声波频率做出反应，就像吉他弦在不同频率下振动产生不同的音符一样。因此，放电率为大脑中的音高知觉提供了另一种编码。这个频率理论解释了基底膜如何加工低于5000赫兹的频率。
p105.en: The neurons on the base membrane react at different frequencies to different acoustic frequencies, as the guitar chords vibrate at different frequencies to produce different notes. Thus, the discharge rate is another code provided by the acoustic perception in the brain. This frequency theory explains how the substrate is processed less than 5000 Hz.

p106.original: 在1000到5000赫兹之间，听觉同时取决于位置和频率。
p106.en: Between 1000 and 5000 Hz, the hearing depends on location and frequency.

p107.original: 1000到5000赫兹的频率范围有什么特别之处？这个区间涵盖了人类语言的高频范围，这对于区分高音的辅音（如p、s和t）至关重要。这些微妙的声音使我们能够区分许多常见的词，如pie（馅饼）、sigh（叹息）、tie（领带）。巧合的是，耳道的特殊形态可以放大这个语音范围内的声音。
p107.en: What's so special about the frequency range of 1,000 to 5,000 Hertz? The zone covers the high frequency range of human languages, which is essential to distinguish high sound from adjoining sound (e.g. p, s and t). These subtle voices allow us to distinguish between many common words, such as pie, sig (sighs), tie. Coincidentally, the special form of the ear is able to magnify the sound in this speech range.

p108.en: It's like a lot of noise.

p109.original: 正如光的强度决定了亮度一样，声波的物理强度或振幅决定了响度，如表3-3所示。更强烈的声波（叫喊声）会产生更大的声音，而小振幅的声波（耳语声）让我们感觉很柔和。因此，振幅是声波的物理特性，而响度是一种心理感觉。
p109.en: Just as the intensity of the light determines the brightness, the physical strength or amplitude of the acoustic wave determines the volume, as shown in Table 3-3. Stronger sound waves (screams) produce greater noise, and small amplifications (ears) make us feel soft. Therefore, amplitude is the physical characteristic of acoustic waves, and the vibration is a psychological feeling.

p110.original: 因为我们可以听到很大强度范围内的声波，所以声音的响度通常用比率而不是绝对量来表示。更具体地说，声强以分贝（dB）为单位表示。图3-14以分贝为单位显示了一些有代表性的自然声音的音量。
p110.en: Because we can hear sound waves in a very strong range, the sound is usually expressed in ratio rather than absolute amount. More specifically, the sound is expressed in dB. Figure 3-14 shows the volume of some representative natural voices in deutsche.

p111.original: 图3-14 某些熟悉声音的强度
p111.en: Figure 3-14: The intensity of certain familiar sounds

p113.original: 狗吠、火车鸣笛的嘟嘟声、双簧管的呜咽声、勺子在杯子里的叮当声都有明显不同，不仅因为它们的音高或响度不同，而且因为它们是不同的特定音调的混合体。事实上，大多数自然声波是混音而不是纯音，如图3-15所示。声波的这种复杂性被称为音色（timbre）。音色这种属性，可以让你在电话中识别朋友的声音，或者区分出不同艺术家演唱的同一首歌。
p113.en: Dog barking, the beeping of train horns, the whizzing of the oboes and the tinkering of spoons in the cups are clearly different, not only because of their high or loudness, but also because they are a mix of different particular sounds. In fact, most natural acoustic waves are mixed rather than pure, as shown in figures 3-15. This complexity of sound waves is known as timbre. This is a quality that allows you to recognize the voice of a friend on the phone, or to distinguish between the same song that different artists sing.

p114.original: 图3-15 某些熟悉声音的波形
p114.en: Figure 3-15 Some waveforms familiar with sound

p115.original: 注：每个声音都是几种纯音的独特组合（Miller，1916/1922）。
p115.en: Note: Each sound is a unique combination of several pure sounds (Miller, 1916/1922).

p117.original: 你的喜欢和熟悉度有关。一项新的大脑成像研究表明，当你听到听起来像另一首你喜欢的曲子的即兴演奏时，位于你大脑中心附近的伏隔核（nucleus accumbens）会向产生奖赏感觉的大脑区域输送一点多巴胺（Salimpoor et al.，2013）。但事实比这要复杂一点，其中还涉及听觉皮层，它分析音乐模式和熟悉程度，以及边缘系统（limbic system）中的情绪加工区域，它们负责判断你对音乐的情绪反应。
p117.en: Your liking and familiarity are related. A new brain imaging study shows that when you hear an improvisation that sounds like another song you like, the nucleus accumbens, located near the center of your brain, can transmit a little dopamine to the brain area that produces a reward (Salimpoor et al., 2013). But the fact is a little more complicated, and it also involves the hearing cortex, which analyzes the music pattern and familiarity, as well as the emotional processing areas in the peripheral system, which are responsible for judging your emotional reaction to music.

p118.original: 瓦莱丽·萨琳普（Valorie Salimpoor）说，不管一首新作品是摇滚乐、布鲁斯乐、古典乐还是嘻哈乐，大脑都会根据你已经熟悉的音乐来理解它。也就是说，大脑试图找到一种模式，并预测音乐将如何播放。如果你以前没听过类似的东西，你的大脑可能就无法预测这种模式，你可能也就无法获得多巴胺的奖赏——这与音乐没什么关系。
p118.en: Valerie Salimpoor said that whether a new piece is rock music, Bruce, classical music or hip-hop, the brain understands it in the light of the music you already know. That is, the brain tries to find a pattern and predicts how music will play. If you've never heard of anything like this before, your brain may not be able to predict this pattern, and you may not be able to get a dopamine reward -- it has nothing to do with music.

p120.original: 年老化和暴露在强噪声中通常会导致听力受损，尤其是对于理解语言至关重要的高频声音。如果你想一想声音b和p之间的细微差别，你就会明白为什么言语知觉如此依赖于高频声音。但听力受损并不全是由于年老化，也可能是因为疾病，如腮腺炎，这种疾病可能会攻击听觉神经。听力受损还可能是由于暴露在强噪声中（见图3-15），例如，枪声、喷气发动机或巨大的音乐声，都有可能损伤耳蜗的毛细胞。
p120.en: Ageing and exposure to high noise usually lead to hearing impairment, especially high frequency voices, which are essential to language understanding. If you think about the slight difference between soundb and p, you'll see why speech is so dependent on high frequency sounds. However, hearing impairment is not due solely to age or possibly to diseases such as mumps, which may attack the hearing nerve. Hearing impairment may also be due to exposure to strong noise (see figure 3-15), for example, gunshots, jet engines or large music sounds, all of which may damage the hair cells of the snails.

p121.original: 现在，听力部分受损的人可以使用高科技助听设备。助听器越来越小，也越来越复杂。一种非常有用的技术是把一个线圈内置到礼堂、出租车或几乎任何其他地点，这样声音可以直接播放到配备了“T线圈”接收器的助听器上。这种配置在欧洲很常见，之后才在美国出现（Munsey，2011）。
p121.en: Now, those who are partially hearing impaired can use high-tech hearing aids. Hearing aids are becoming smaller and more complex. A very useful technique is to place a wire inside the auditorium, taxi or almost any other location, so that the sound can be played directly onto a hearing aid equipped with a "T-ring" receiver. This configuration is common in Europe, but only after its appearance in the United States (Munsey, 2011).

p122.original: 有一种被称为耳蜗植入术的手术，可以为听力严重受损但听神经功能正常的人恢复部分听力。人工耳蜗本身就是一根穿过耳蜗的电线，通过电脉冲直接刺激听神经（见图3-16）。接受过植入手术的人报告说声音和正常听力不一样。然而，在通常情况下，这种手术能够让他们听懂言语，甚至欣赏音乐，这在手术前是不可能的（National Institutes of Health，2014）。
p122.en: There is an operation known as a cochlear implant that restores a partial hearing to a person whose hearing is severely impaired but whose hearing function is normal. The cochlear itself is a wire through which the earring directly stimulates the hearing through a pulse (see figure 3-16). Those who have undergone implant surgery report that their voices are not the same as normal hearing. However, in general, this operation enables them to understand words and even to appreciate music, which is not possible before the operation (National Institutes of Health, 2014).

p124.original: 注：一根电线将来自外部接收器的声音信息通过头骨直接传送到耳蜗，让一些听力严重受损的人再次听到声音。
p124.en: Note: An electrical wire transmits sound messages from an external receiver directly through the skull to the snail, allowing some people with severe hearing impairment to hear the sound again.

p125.original: 3.5.6 听觉和视觉感觉的相似性
p125.en: 3.5.6 Similarity of hearing and visual perceptions

p126.original: 之前，我们讨论了视觉信息如何通过视神经以神经脉冲的形式传递到大脑。现在我们发现，听觉信息也以类似的方式作为神经信号传递给大脑，只是传输途径不同，到达大脑的位置也不同。请注意视觉和听觉利用光波和声波中的频率和振幅信息的方式有其相似性。
p126.en: Before that, we discussed how visual information is transmitted to the brain through the optic nerve in the form of a nerve pulse. Now we find that hearing information is transmitted to the brain in a similar way as a neural signal, except that the transmission route is different and the location of the brain is different. Note the similarity of visual and hearing use of frequency and amplitude information in light and sound waves.

p127.original: 但为什么我们是“看到”视觉信息，而“听到”听觉信息？正如我们在核心概念3.2所指出的，答案在于接收神经信息的皮层区域不同，而不是信息本身的某种独特性质。总之，大脑不同区域在被激活时会产生不同的感觉。
p127.en: But why are we "seeing" visual information and "hearing" hearing information? As we have pointed out in the core concept 3.2, the answer lies in the fact that the cortical regions that receive neural information are different, not in the unique nature of the information itself. In short, different regions of the brain have different feelings when activated.

p128.original: 3.6 对比视觉、听觉和其他感觉
p128.en: 3.6 Comparison of visual, hearing and other feelings

p130.original: 解释本体觉、运动觉、嗅觉、味觉、皮肤感觉和痛觉等感觉是如何工作的。描述视觉和听觉的相似性。
p130.en: Explain how the instincts, exercise, smell, taste, skin feeling and pain work. Describe the similarity of vision and hearing.

p131.original: 在我们的所有感觉中，视觉和听觉被研究得最多。然而，我们的生存和幸福也依赖于其他感觉。因此，在结束对感觉的讨论之前，我们将简要综述本体觉、运动觉、嗅觉、味觉、皮肤感觉和痛觉所涉及的加工过程（见表3-4）。
p131.en: In all our feelings, vision and hearing are most studied. However, our survival and well-being also depend on other feelings. Therefore, before concluding our discussion of feelings, we will briefly provide an overview of the processes involved in the process of innuendo, exercise, smell, taste, skin feeling and pain (see tables 3-4).

p132.original: 表3-4 人类感觉的基础特征
p132.en: Table 3-4 Basic characteristics of human perception

p133.original: 你会注意到，每种感觉都给了我们关于我们内部或外部环境的不同方面的信息。然而，它们的运作原理相似。每一种感觉系统都将物理刺激转导为神经活动，而且每种感觉对变化刺激比对恒定刺激更敏感。另外，就像视觉和听觉一样，每种感觉都是通过它所提取的信息类型和大脑中专门加工信息的区域来区分的。最后，感觉往往是协调一致的，我们看到闪电的时候会听到雷声，而我们称之为“味觉”的感觉其实是食物的色、香、味和质地的组合体。尝尝发出滋滋声响的铁板牛排、冒着气泡的可乐或脆米花，你很容易发现其中的感觉组合。
p133.en: You will note that every feeling gives us information on the different aspects of our internal or external environment. However, they operate in a similar manner. Each sensory system transfers physical stimulation to neuroactivity, and each is more sensitive to change stimulation than to constant stimulation. Moreover, as with visual and hearing, each feeling is distinguished by the type of information it extracts and by the area of information specifically processed in the brain. Finally, feelings tend to be consistent, and thunders are heard when we see lightning, and what we call a taste is actually a combination of the colour, aroma, taste and texture of food. You can easily find a combination of the chorus steaks, the bubbled Cokes or the crumbs.

p135.original: 我们的行动是有目的的，还要不失优雅，因此我们需要不断更新我们的四肢和身体其他部位相对于彼此和环境中物体的位置。没有这些信息，即使是最简单的行动也不可能协调起来（你可能有过试图在一条腿麻木时走路的经历）。跟踪身体位置、运动和平衡的物理机制实际上涉及两个不同的系统：前庭觉（vestibular sense）和运动觉（kinesthetic sense）。
p135.en: Our actions are purposeful and elegant, and we need to constantly update the position of our limbs and other parts of our body vis-à-vis each other and objects in the environment. Without this information, even the simplest actions cannot be coordinated (you may have had an experience trying to walk in a numb leg). The physical mechanism for tracking physical position, movement and balance actually involves two different systems: pre-mortem (vestibular sense) and kinesthetic sense (kinesty sense).

p136.original: 前庭觉是一种身体位置的感觉，帮助我们相对于重力来定向。它告诉我们身体的姿势，无论是直的、前俯的、后仰的，还是倒置的。前庭感觉也告诉我们什么时候在运动或者我们的运动是如何变化的。这些信息的感受器是内耳半规管中的细毛（很像我们在基底膜中发现的那些，参见图3-13）。这些毛发通过检测半规管中液体的运动来对身体的运动做出反应。这种感觉出现障碍会导致极度眩晕和迷失方向。
p136.en: The aforethought is a feeling of physical location that helps us to be directed against gravity. It tells us the position of the body, whether it be straight, forward, backward, or upside down. The Tribunal felt like telling us when to move or how to change our movement. The sensor for this information is the hair in the inner ear and half of the tube (like what we found in the substrate, see figures 3-13). These hairs react to body movements by detecting movement of liquids in semi-regulated systems. This perception of an obstacle can lead to extreme dizziness and loss of direction.

p137.original: 运动觉是身体位置和运动的另一种感觉，它跟踪身体各部位之间的相对关系。例如，你的运动觉会让你意识到你在双腿交叉，并在手机响的时候告诉你哪只手离手机更近。运动觉提供持续的感觉反馈，告诉你在运动和活动过程中身体的肌肉在做什么，例如，你是要继续伸手拿咖啡杯，还是要在你把咖啡杯打翻之前停止动作（Turvey，1996）。
p137.en: Momentopathy is another feeling of physical location and movement, which tracks the relative relationship between the various parts of the body. For example, your sense of exercise will make you realize that you cross your legs and tell you which hand is closer to your cell phone when it rings. Momentopathy provides continuous feedback on what the body muscles are doing during exercise and activity, for example, whether to reach for coffee cups or to stop before you turn them over (Turvey, 1996).

p138.original: 体操运动员和舞蹈演员依靠他们的前庭觉和运动觉来获得有关身体位置和运动的信息。
p138.en: Gymnasticians and dancers rely on their pre-sensitization and exercise to obtain information about their physical location and sports.

p139.original: 运动觉感受器位于关节、肌肉和肌腱中。这些感受器，以及前庭觉的感受器，连接着大脑顶叶（parietal lobes）的加工区域——该脑区帮助我们制作物体和事件之间空间关系的感觉“地图”。这一类加工通常会下意识地、自动地、毫不费力地进行，除非我们在学习一项新的身体技能，在有意地练习动作，例如，挥舞高尔夫球杆或演奏乐器。
p139.en: Motion sensor is in the joints, muscles and muscles. These sensors, together with the exterior sensor, are connected to the processing area of the upper lobes of the brain, which helps us to create a sense of “maps” of space relations between objects and events. This type of processing is usually carried out unconsciously, automatically and without effort unless we are learning a new physical skill and are intentionally practicing actions such as swinging golf clubs or playing musical instruments.

p141.original: 嗅觉（olfaction）具有保护性的功能，因为嗅觉可以感知可能有害的食物的气味，某些动物还可以感知捕食者的气味。我们人类似乎主要利用嗅觉和味觉来定位和识别高热量食物，避免食用受污染的食物，而且似乎还能识别潜在的伴侣——香水行业很好地利用了这一点（Benson，2002；Martins et al.，2005；Miller & Maner，2010）。
p141.en: A sense of smell is protective because it can sense the odour of potentially harmful food, and some animals can sense the odour of predators. We humans seem to use our senses of smell and taste to locate and identify high-heat foods, avoid eating contaminated foods, and also seem to identify potential partners, which is well used in the perfume industry (Benson, 2002); Martins et al., 2005; Miller & Maner, 2010.

p142.original: 许多动物对嗅觉的利用更进一步，它们用嗅觉来进行交流。例如，昆虫（如蚂蚁和白蚁）和脊椎动物（如狗和猫）通过分泌和检测气味信号［称为信息素（pheromones）］来相互交流，特别是发出性接受信号，以及危险、领地边界、食物来源和家庭成员的信号。在更有限的范围内，人类也能这样交流，尽管事实证明我们很难确定其中所涉及的确切化学物质（Blum，2011）。玛莎·麦克林托克（Martha McClintock，1971）在一篇著名的论文中首次提出了这种效应，该论文表明，女性在一起生活（就像在大学宿舍里一样）几个月后，其月经周期会趋于同步，尽管作者无法确定引起同步的化学物质。随后的研究表明，婴儿更习惯母亲穿过的衣服的气味。其他研究发现，人们可以区分观看恐怖电影的志愿者和观看喜剧电影志愿者的汗液样本（Zhou & Chen，2009）。而那些嗅到女性泪滴的男性，睾丸激素水平会突然下降，同时性兴趣也会减弱（Gelstein et al.，2011）。从逻辑上讲，这些研究中的信号一定是信息素化学物质，但所涉及哪些物质仍然是个谜。
p142.en: Many animals use their sense of smell even further, and they use it to communicate. For example, insects (e.g. ants and termites) and vertebrates (e.g. dogs and cats) communicate with each other through the distribution and detection of odour signals [known as pheromones], in particular through sexual acceptance signals, as well as signals from hazards, territorial boundaries, food sources and family members. On a more limited scale, humans can communicate as well, although it has proved difficult to identify the exact chemical substances involved (Blum, 2011). Martha McClintock, 1971, presented this effect for the first time in a well-known paper, which showed that women lived together (as in university dormitories) for several months and their menstruation cycles tended to synchronize, although the author was unable to identify the chemicals that caused the synchronization. Subsequent studies have shown that babies are more accustomed to the smell of clothing that their mothers wear. Other studies have found that it is possible to distinguish between sweat samples of volunteers watching horror films and volunteers watching comedy films (Zhou & Chen, 2009). Men who smell women's tears will suddenly decline their testosterone levels and their sexual interest will diminish (Gelstein et al., 2011). Logically, the signals in these studies must be informational chemicals, but the substances involved remain a mystery.

p144.original: 从生物学上讲，嗅觉是从鼻子里的化学活动开始的。在那里，气味（以空气中化学分子的形式）与特定神经细胞相关的感受器蛋白相互作用（Axel，1995；Turin，2006）。顺便说一句，这些细胞是人体唯一与外界环境直接接触的神经细胞。
p144.en: Biologically, the smell begins with chemical activity in the nose. There, the smell (in the form of chemical molecules in the air) interacts with the sensory protein associated with specific neurons (Axel, 1995); Turin, 2006. By the way, these cells are the only neurons in the human body that are in direct contact with the outside environment.

p145.original: 气味分子复杂多样。例如，新煮的咖啡的香气包含多达600种挥发性化合物（Wilson & Stevenson，2006）。目前为止，科学家们已经区分了至少1500种不同的可以产生气味的分子（Zimmer，2010）。现在还不完全清楚鼻子究竟是如何处理这些纷杂的气味的，但我们确实知道，鼻腔感受器能感觉气味分子的形状（Foley & Matlin，2010）。
p145.en: The odor molecule is complex and diverse. For example, fresh coffee is fragrance containing up to 600 volatile compounds (Wilson & Stevenson, 2006). So far, scientists have distinguished at least 1,500 different molecules that can produce a scent (Zimmer, 2010). It's not entirely clear how the nose handles these odours, but we do know that the nasal sensor can feel the shape of the odor molecule (Foley & Matlin, 2010).

p146.original: 我们还知道，鼻子的感受器细胞会转导有关刺激的信息，并将其传递给大脑的嗅球。嗅球位于大脑下部，在额叶的正下方（见图3-17）。我们的嗅觉最初在嗅球进行加工，然后传递到大脑的许多其他部分（Mori et al.，1999）。与所有其他感官不同，嗅觉信号不通过丘脑传递，这表明嗅觉有着非常古老的进化根源。
p146.en: We also know that the sensory cells in the nose can shift the information about the stimulation and pass it to the sniffing ball in the brain. The sniffing ball is located in the lower part of the brain and directly below the forehead (see figure 3-17). Our sense of smell is first processed in the sniffing ball and then passed to many other parts of the brain (Mori et al., 1999). Unlike all other senses, the fact that smell signals are not transmitted through the crochet indicates that the sense of smell has very old evolutionary roots.

p147.original: 图3-17 嗅觉感受器（Zimbardo & Gerrig，1999）

p149.original: 嗅觉与情绪及记忆有着密切的联系。这也许可以解释为什么嗅球非常靠近边缘系统和颞叶中与情绪、记忆相关的结构，并与之直接交流。因此，我们也就不会奇怪于心理学家和作家所注意到的，某些气味能唤起充满情感的记忆，有时则会使人想起被遗忘的事件（Dingfelder，2004）。想一想，说不定你的脑中就会浮现出某种香味的生动形象的记忆，来自你童年时最喜欢的食物，例如新鲜的面包或辛辣的菜肴。
p149.en: The sense of smell is closely linked to emotions and memories. This may explain why the sniffing ball is very close to, and communicates directly with, emotional, memory-related structures in peripheral systems and leaves. Thus, we are not surprised by what psychologists and writers have noticed, that certain scents can inspire emotional memories and sometimes remind people of forgotten events (Dingfelder, 2004). Think about it, you may have some kind of vivid image in your head that comes from your favorite childhood foods, such as fresh bread or spicy dishes.

p152.original: 你能想到一种可以唤起你记忆的气味吗？描述你与那种气味联系在一起的记忆，并探究为什么你认为这种记忆非常强大。
p152.en: Can you think of a smell that can lift your memory? Describe your memories associated with that smell and explore why you think they are very powerful.

p154.original: 如同嗅觉，味觉也是一种基于化学反应的感觉。但两者的相似性不止于此，味觉和嗅觉之间有着密切合作的伙伴关系——许多你可能认为是味道的细微差别其实都来自于气味。（洋葱的“味道”大部分是气味，而不是味道。当你感冒时，你会发现食物索然无味，那是因为你的鼻腔阻塞了。）
p154.en: Like smell, taste is also a chemical-based feeling. But the similarities between the two are more than that, and there is a close partnership between taste and smell — many of the nuances that you may think are from the smell. (The onion's taste is mostly smell, not smell. When you catch a cold, you find the food is dry, because your nasal cavity is blocked. I don't think so.

p155.original: 大多数人都知道，我们主要有四种味觉（gustation）：甜、酸、苦、咸。然而，还有鲜为人知的第五种味道叫鲜味（Chaudhari et al.，2000）。鲜味是在诸如肉、海鲜和奶酪等富含蛋白质的食物中发现的一种风味。鲜味还与味精有关，味精常用于亚洲菜肴。
p155.en: Most people know that we have four main tastes: sweet, acid, bitter, salty. However, there is a fifth little known taste (Chaudhari et al., 2000). The smell is found in protein-rich foods such as meat, seafood and cheese. The smell is also related to the smelt, which is often used in Asian dishes.

p156.original: 味觉的感受器细胞位于舌头上面和侧面的味蕾中，在食物和饮料进入胃的过程中对它们进行取样。如图3-18所示，这些味觉感受器聚集在称为舌乳头的小黏膜突起里，每个都对特定形状的分子特别敏感。
p156.en: Taste sensor cells are located in taste buds on the top and side of the tongue and are sampled as food and beverages enter the stomach. As can be seen in figures 3-18, these oscillator sensors are concentrated in the sprawling of a little mucous membrane called tongue nipples, each of which is particularly sensitive to molecules of a particular shape.

p158.original: 除了舌头上的感受器之外，一条专门的神经“热线”把味觉信息传送到大脑皮层的专门区域。味觉是在顶叶的躯体感觉区实现的。顺带说一下，这一区域位于接受面部触觉刺激的皮层附近（Gadsby，2000）。
p158.en: In addition to the sensor on the tongue, a special nerve “hotline” transmits odour information to specialized areas of the cortex of the brain. Taste is done in the body area of the top leaves. By the way, this area is located near the cortical layer receiving facial sensory irritation (Gadsby, 2000).

p159.en: The evolution of the taste system

p160.original: 婴儿的味觉敏感度较高，所以婴儿普遍不喜欢柠檬的苦味。然而，这种超敏感性随着年龄的增长而降低。因此，许多老年人抱怨食物没有味道，这实际上是因为他们感觉能力下降，而无法察觉食物的味道和气味的差异。此外，味觉感受器很容易被酒精、烟、酸或热的食物破坏。幸运的是，我们经常更新味觉感受器，就像更新嗅觉感受器一样。由于不断更新，味觉系统是我们所有感觉中最能抵抗永久性损伤的，完全丧失味觉的情况极为罕见（Bartoshuk，1990）。
p160.en: Babies are more sensitive to taste, so they generally do not like the bitter taste of lemon. However, this super-sensitivity decreases with age. As a result, many older persons complain about the lack of food, which is in fact because they feel less capable of detecting differences in the taste and smell of food. In addition, a taste sensor can be easily destroyed by alcohol, smoke, acid or hot food. Fortunately, we often update the taste sensor, like the smell sensor. As a result of continuous updating, the taste system is the most resistant to permanent damage in all our senses, and total loss of taste is extremely rare (Bartoshuk, 1990).

p161.original: 超级味觉者的“霓虹”世界
p161.en: The Neon World of Super Tasteors.

p162.original: 不同年龄的个体对味觉的敏感程度不同，这跟舌乳头的密度有关（Bartoshuk，2000，2009；Bartoshuk et al.，1994）。那些拥有最多味蕾的人是超级味觉者，他们生活在相对于我们其他人来说的一个“霓虹”味觉世界中，这也解释了为什么他们讨厌某些食物，如西兰花或“健康”饮料，这些食物中的苦味令他们不爽（Duenwald，2005）。做一个超级味觉者有什么好处吗？味觉专家琳达·巴托舒克（Linda Bartoshuk，1993）认为，由于大多数有毒物质都是苦的，所以超级味觉者更具有生存优势。
p162.en: The sensitivity of individuals of different ages to tastes varies, which is related to the density of tongue nipples (Bartoshuk, 2000, 2009); Bartoshuk et al., 1994. Those who have the most taste buds are super-savory people, who live in a neon-savored world compared to the rest of us, which explains why they hate certain foods, such as broccoli or “healthy” drinks, the bitter taste of which makes them uncomfortable (Duenwald, 2005). What good is it to be a super-savory person? Linda Bartoshuk, a taste expert, believes that since most toxic substances are bitter, supersystemists have the advantage of survival.

p163.original: 这种差异也说明了我们在本章伊始特别提到的问题，即不同的人是否会以同样的方式来感觉世界。巴托舒克的研究表明，在某种程度上，感觉感受器在不同的人之间表现出某种差异，我们对世界的感觉体验也是如此。有这种差异并不奇怪，这使得某个人的甜的感觉和另一个人的酸的感觉是一样的。不过，主要的差异表现在味觉的强度上，例如，超级味觉者觉察到的苦味。根据巴托舒克的说法，一个未知的问题是人们对不同味觉的敏感度是否不同，例如，一个人是否可以在品尝苦味时是超级味觉者，而对甜味或咸味只有正常的感觉（personal communication，January 4，2011）。
p163.en: This difference also illustrates the question that we mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, namely, whether different people feel the world in the same way. The Bartoshuk study shows that, to some extent, the sensor manifests a certain difference between people, as do our experience of the world. It is not surprising that there is such a difference that one feels the same sweetness as another. However, the main differences are reflected in the intensity of the taste, for example, the bitterness felt by the supersensor. According to Batoshuk, an unknown question is whether people are sensitive to different tastes, for example, whether a person can be supersympathetic when tasted bitter, while the taste of sweetness or salt is normal (personic communification, January 4, 2011).

p164.original: 另一方面，味觉研究人员发现，超级味觉者和正常味觉者的味觉偏好存在差异。特别是，超级味觉者更经常报告不喜欢的食物，他们会觉得太甜或有太多脂肪。尽管这一点仍有待确定，但研究人员观察到，平均而言，超级味觉者的体重比非超级味觉者要轻（Bartoshuk，2000）。
p164.en: On the other hand, taste researchers have found differences between the taste preferences of the supersensor and the normal. In particular, super-sympathetics report more often on food that they do not like, and they feel too sweet or have too much fat. Although this remains to be determined, researchers have observed that on average the weight of the supersystolics is lighter than that of non-supersystolics (Bartoshuk, 2000).

p166.original: 皮肤具有多种非凡的功能，它能保护我们免受表面伤害，保留体液，并有助于调节体温。皮肤还含有神经末梢，当受到刺激时，会产生触觉、痛觉、温暖和寒冷的感觉。像其他几种感觉一样，这些皮肤感觉（skin senses）与位于大脑顶叶的躯体感觉皮层（somatosensory cortex）相连（见图3-19）。
p166.en: Skin has a variety of extraordinary functions that protect us from surface damage, preserve body fluids and help regulate body temperature. The skin also contains nerve endings, which, when irritated, give rise to feelings of touch, pain, warmth and cold. As with several other feelings, these skin feelings (skin senses) are linked to the body cortex (somatosensory cotex) located at the top of the brain (see figures 3-19).

p168.original: 注：图中身体部位的相对大小对应于身体各部位专用于触觉的皮层数量。
p168.en: Note: The relative size of body parts in the figure corresponds to the number of cortex parts of the body that are specifically used for tactile purposes.

p169.original: 我们的躯体对刺激的敏感度变化很大，这部分取决于每个区域的感受器数量。例如，我们在感觉指尖的刺激时比感觉背部的刺激敏锐10倍。总体来说，我们的敏感度在最需要的地方是最高的，即脸、舌头和手上。对躯体这些部位的精确感觉反馈让我们能有效地进食、说话和抓握。
p169.en: Our body's sensitivity to stimulation has changed significantly, depending in part on the number of sensors per region. For example, we feel the sharpness of the tip of the finger when it comes to the back. In general, our sensitivity is highest where it is most needed, namely, the face, tongue and hand. The feedback on these parts of the body allows us to feed, speak and hold effectively.

p170.original: 触觉在人际关系中起着核心作用，这体现了皮肤敏感的重要性。通过触觉，我们传达了给予或接受安慰、支持和爱的愿望（Fisher，1992；Harlow，1965）。触觉也是人类性唤起的主要刺激。抚触对身心健康发展至关重要；缺乏触觉刺激会阻碍儿童的智力和运动发展（Anand & Scalzo，2000）。
p170.en: Touches play a central role in interpersonal relations, which reflects the importance of skin sensitivity. Through touch, we convey our desire to give or accept comfort, support and love (Fisher, 1992); Harlow, 1965. Touches are also a major stimulus to humanity. Touching is essential for the development of physical and mental health; Lack of tactile stimulation can hinder children's intellectual and physical development (Anand & Scalzo, 2000).

p173.original: 我们会暴露在许多我们的感觉无法察觉的刺激之下。说出其中一种，并解释为什么我们检测不到它。（提示：想想我们用来检测感觉“窗口”之外的信息的电子或机械设备。）
p173.en: We'll be exposed to a lot of undetectable irritation. Say one of them and explain why we can't detect it. (Tips: Think of the electronic or mechanical devices that we use to detect information outside the perceived window. I don't think so.

p176.original: 关于大脑的感觉加工机制，解释联觉能教给我们什么。
p176.en: About the brain's sensory process, explain what the synergetics can teach us.

p177.original: 少数“正常”的人有一种被称为联觉（synesthesia）的情况，这种情况允许他们跨感觉领域感觉自己的世界。实际上，有些人尝出了形状的感觉，例如，梨尝起来是“圆”的，西柚是“尖”的（Cytowic，1993）。有些联觉者（包括本书作者之一）则会把一周中的星期几和颜色联系起来，所以星期三可能是“绿色”，星期四可能是“红色”。联觉的定义性特征就是将一种感觉与另一种感觉结合起来的感觉体验。
p177.en: A small number of “normal” people have a situation called synesthesia, which allows them to feel their world across the realm of feeling. In fact, some people taste shapes, for example, pears taste “round” and grapefruits are “tight” (Cytowic, 1993). Some of the cosmonauts (including one of the authors of the book) link the number of weeks and the colours of the week, so Wednesday may be “green” and Thursday may be “red”. The definitional characteristic of synergism is the experience of combining one feeling with another.

p178.original: 通过巧妙的实验，V. S.拉马钱德兰（V. S. Ramachandran）和他的同事已经证明，联觉中的交叉感觉是真实的，而不仅仅是隐喻（Ramachandran & Hubbard，2001）。你可以在随后的“试一试”版块中参加他们的一个测试。研究还表明，这种能力出现在多个家庭成员身上，因此联觉可能有遗传成分。
p178.en: V. S. Ramachandran and his colleagues have demonstrated through a clever experiment that the intersection of the feeling in the connection is real and not just metaphorical (Ramachandran & Hubbard, 2001). You can take a test of them in the subsequent "tried" section. The study also showed that this capability occurs in multiple family members and that there may be a genetic component to the sensory.

p179.original: 联觉是什么导致的？显然，这可能涉及加工不同感觉的不同脑区之间的交流，这些区域通常在大脑皮层中彼此相邻。脑成像研究表明，在颞叶、顶叶和枕叶的交界处有一个被称为TPO的皮层区域（Ramachandran & Hubbard，2003）。这个区域同时加工来自许多通路的信息。拉马钱德兰认为，我们每个人的这些区域之间都有一些神经联系，但联觉者似乎比大多数人有更多的联系。
p179.en: What's the connection? Obviously, this may involve processing exchanges between different brain regions with different perceptions, which are usually adjacent to each other in the cortex of the brain. A study of brain imaging shows that there is a cortex area known as TPO at the intersection of the leaf, caps and pillows (Ramachandran & Hubbard, 2003). This area also processes information from many routes. Ramachandran believes that there are some neurological links between these areas of each of us, but the communicators seem to have more connections than most.

p180.original: 拉马钱德兰断言，这种情况在创造力强的人身上发生得稍微多一些。这也许可以解释一些神秘主义者在人们周围看到的“光环”（Holden，2004）。但也许我们都有一些跨感觉的能力，这也许就是为什么我们会对莎士比亚在《罗密欧与朱丽叶》中的著名比喻产生共鸣：“那是东方，而朱丽叶就是太阳。”当然，我们知道他说的不是字面意思。相反，我们明白，对罗密欧和我们来说，朱丽叶是与光、温暖和愉悦感联系在一起的（Ramachandran & Hirstein，1999）。
p180.en: Ramachandran asserted that this happened slightly more among creative people. This may explain what some mystics see around people in the `Holden' (2004). But perhaps we all have some cross-friable powers, and that's probably why we resonate with Shakespeare's famous metaphor in Romeo and Juliet: "It's the East, and Juliet is the Sun. “Of course, we know that what he's saying is not literally. On the contrary, we understand that for Romeo and for us, Juliet is associated with light, warmth and pleasure (Ramahandran & Hirstein, 1999).

p181.original: 你可以通过麦格（McGurk）错觉来体验不同感觉之间的相互影响。这种错觉说明了大脑是如何将来自不同感觉的信息组合成一个连贯的整体的。正如你看到（和听到）的，即使在视觉和听觉信息冲突时，大脑仍然完成了一个了不起的整合。
p181.en: You can experience the interaction between different feelings through the idea of McGurk. This illusion illustrates how the brain combines information from different feelings into a coherent whole. As you see (and hear), even when visual and hearing information clashs, the brain has achieved a remarkable integration.

p183.original: 大多数人在盯着十字架的时候可以毫无困难地看到数字5（见图3-20中的左图），但当5被其他数字包围时会变得模糊（见图3-20中的右图）。但是，如果你是一个将颜色与数字联系起来的联觉者，你通常就能识别右图中的5，因为它看起来是与该数字相联系的色块（Ramachandran & Hubbard，2003）。
p183.en: Most people can see the number 5 without difficulty while staring at the cross (see the left figure in figure 3-20), but it becomes blurred when they are surrounded by other figures (see the right figure in figure 3-20). However, if you are a sensor that links the colour to the number, you will normally be able to identify the five in the right picture because it appears to be the colour of the number (Ramahandran & Hubbard, 2003).

p184.en: Figure 3-20. Do you have a connection?

p185.original: 注：当你凝视十字架时，你能看到“5”吗？两个图里都能看到吗？
p185.en: Note: When you stare at the cross, can you see Five? Can you see them both?

p186.original: 心理学很有用 疼痛的感觉和体验
p186.en: Psychology works. Pain feels and experiences.

p187.original: 如果你在承受剧痛，那么其他什么都不重要。伤口或牙痛会压倒所有其他感觉。有三分之一的美国人遭受过持续或反复疼痛的折磨，这种经历会使人虚弱不堪，有时甚至会导致自杀。然而，疼痛也是身体适应机制的一部分，它使人们对威胁身体健康的情况做出反应。
p187.en: If you're suffering, nothing else matters. A wound or toothache overwhelms all other feelings. One third of Americans have suffered from constant or repeated pain, a experience that has weakened people and sometimes led to suicide. However, pain is also part of the physical adaptation mechanism, which allows people to respond to situations that threaten their health.

p188.original: 与其他感觉不同，疼痛可以由各种强烈的刺激引起，如非常响亮的声音、沉重的压力、针刺或非常明亮的光线。但是疼痛不仅仅是刺激的结果。它也受到我们的情绪和期望的影响，如果你害怕看牙医，那么你就会知道这一点（Koyama et al.，2005）。
p188.en: Unlike other feelings, pain can be caused by a variety of strong irritations, such as very loud voices, heavy stress, needles or very bright light. But pain is not just the result of irritation. It is also influenced by our emotions and expectations, and if you are afraid to see a dentist, you will know that (Koyama et al., 2005).

p190.original: 在皮肤中，有几种被称为痛觉感受器（nociceptor）的特殊神经细胞，能感觉到疼痛的刺激，并将其不愉快的信息传送到中枢神经系统。一些痛觉感受器对热最敏感，而另一些则主要对压力、化学创伤或其他组织损伤做出反应（Foley & Matlin，2010）。甚至还有专门感受瘙痒的痛觉感受器，瘙痒本身也是一种疼痛（Gieler & Walter，2008）。
p190.en: In the skin, there are several special neurons known as pain sensor (nociceptor), which can feel the irritation of pain and transmit its unpleasant information to the central nervous system. Some pain sensors are the most sensitive to heat, while others respond mainly to stress, chemical trauma or other tissue damage (Foley & Matlin, 2010). There are even a pain sensor specializing in itching, which in itself is a pain (Gieler & Walter, 2008).

p192.original: 尽管疼痛可能来自离大脑很远的身体部位，但我们确实是在大脑中感受到疼痛的。至少有两个不同的区域加工传入的疼痛信息（Foley & Matlin，2010；Porreca & Price，2009）。其中一个区域涉及一条终止于顶叶的通路，该区域记录疼痛的位置、强度和剧烈程度。另一个区域是位于额叶皮层（frontal cortex）、丘脑和边缘系统深处的一组结构，该区域记录疼痛的感觉有多么不愉快。第二个区域受损的人可能会感受到疼痛刺激，但会报告说没有感到不愉快。
p192.en: Although pain may come from parts of the body far from the brain, we do feel pain in the brain. At least two different regions processed imported pain information (Foley & Matlin, 2010); Porreca & Price, 2009. One of these areas involves a road that ends at the top and records the location, intensity and intensity of the pain. Another area is a group of structures located deep in frontal cortex, cortex and periphery systems, where pain is being recorded in an unpleasant manner. People who are damaged in the second area may feel pain and irritation, but are not unhappy.

p194.original: 关于痛觉的一个谜团涉及失去手臂或腿的人经常经历的神秘感觉，这种情况被称为幻肢。在这种情况下，截肢者有时会感觉相当痛苦，而疼痛似乎来自身体缺失的部位（Ramachandran & Blakeslee，1998）。神经学研究表明，幻肢的感觉并非源于感觉通路中的神经受损。它们也不是纯粹的想象。相反，幻肢的感觉源于大脑本身，是大脑产生感觉的结果，因为感觉不可能来自缺失的肢体（Dingfelder，2007）。幻肢的奇怪现象告诉我们，理解疼痛不仅需要理解疼痛的感觉，还需要理解大脑中加工和抑制疼痛的机制。
p194.en: A mystery about pain relates to the mysterious feeling that people who lose their arms or legs often experience, a situation called phantom limbs. In such cases, amputees sometimes feel considerable pain, which appears to come from parts of the body that are missing (Ramahandran & Blakeslee, 1998). Neurological studies show that the feeling of phantom limbs does not stem from the sense of neural damage on the road. They are not mere imaginations. On the contrary, the feeling of a phantom limb is the result of the brain itself, which produces the feeling, since it cannot be from a missing limb (Dingfeld, 2007). The strange phenomenon of phantom limbs tells us that understanding pain requires not only understanding the feeling of pain, but also the mechanisms for processing and containing it in the brain.

p196.original: 我们早就知道，人们对事件的解释会影响刺激是否被认为是疼痛刺激（Turk，1994）。因此，运动员遭受严重的伤害后，却觉得不是很疼，直到比赛的兴奋结束才会有较强的感觉。另外，当人们认为安慰剂（placebos）（“糖丸”）或其他假治疗是真的时，慢性疼痛可能会得到缓解。
p196.en: We knew long ago that the interpretation of events would affect whether irritation was considered pain irritation (Turk, 1994). As a result, athletes do not feel much pain after having suffered serious injuries until the excitement of the game is over. In addition, chronic pain may be alleviated when placebos ( "sugar pills") or other false treatment is considered to be genuine.

p197.original: 疼痛的闸门控制理论（gate-control theory）是我们对这些“心重于身”的现象的最好解释（Melzack & Wall，1965，1983）。要理解其原理，不要忘了痛觉是从对强烈刺激或伤害敏感的、被称为痛觉感受器的特殊神经元涌向大脑的。大多数疼痛信号是从痛觉感受器通过脊髓的一条优先通路传递到大脑的。可以通过打开或关闭疼痛的脊髓通路中的神经“门”来阻断或促进疼痛。这可以通过大脑发出的“自上而下”的信息来实现，该信息可以源于一个人的情绪状态或其他精神干扰（Strobel et al.，2014），想一下某个在激烈的战斗中没有注意到伤口的士兵。同样，催眠可以打开和关闭脊髓门，催眠的效果让大脑向下发出指令，关闭脊髓门（Fields，2009）。在催眠状态下，关闭闸门以阻断疼痛被认为涉及特殊的中间神经元，这些中间神经元将信息从大脑“自上而下”传递到脊髓中的疼痛通道。“关门”意味着大脑发出信号抑制脊髓通路中传入的疼痛信息。
p197.en: The pain-control theory (gate-control theory) is the best explanation for these “heart-to-heart” phenomena (Melzack & Wall, 1965, 1983). To understand its rationale, it is important not to forget that pain flows to the brain from special neurons that are sensitive to strong irritation or injury, known as pain sensors. Most pain signals are transmitted to the brain from the pain sensor through a priority route to the spinal cord. Pain can be broken or facilitated by opening or closing the neuro- “doors” in the spinal circuits of pain. This can be achieved by a “top-down” message from the brain, which can be derived from a person's emotional state or other mental disturbance (Strobel et al., 2014), thinking about a soldier who did not notice the wound in a fierce battle. Similarly, hypnosis opens and closes the spinal doors, and the effect of hypnosis is to give the brain a downward direction to close the spinal doors (Filds, 2009). Under hypnosis, the closing of the gates to stop pain is considered to involve special intermediate neurons that transmit information from the brain “top-down” to the pain channel in the spinal cord. “Closed” means that the brain sends a signal to suppress the pain that flows through the spinal circuits.

p198.original: 还有什么可以关闭脊髓门？阿片类镇痛药，如吗啡，也可以通过从大脑中的特殊内啡肽受体引发一连串抑制信息，从而“自上而下”地发挥作用。这些抑制性信息向下传递以“关闭闸门”而阻止疼痛信息上传。
p198.en: What else can we close the spinal cord door? Opioid analgesics, such as morphine, can also function “top-down” by triggering a chain of inhibitive messages from special endorphins in the brain. These inhibiting messages are transmitted downwards to prevent the uploading of pain messages by “closing the gates”.

p199.original: 至少有一种方法可以“自下而上”地关闭疼痛之门，并且不涉及大脑。在疼痛信息通过脊髓的平行路径上传时，来自非痛觉感受器（例如，那些与触觉有关的感受器）的强烈刺激被认为可以抑制或压制疼痛信息。这就解释了为什么当你被锤子敲到手指后用力握手会让疼痛得以缓解（Carlson，2007）。针灸的作用方式大致相同，它向脊髓发送相互竞争的“自下而上”的信号。
p199.en: There is at least one way to close the door to pain “bottom-up” and not to involve the brain. When pain information is uploaded through parallel paths to the spinal cord, strong stimulation from non-aching sensors (e.g., sensory-related sensors) is considered to inhibit or suppress pain information. This explains why handshakes when you get hammered on your finger can relieve pain (Carlson, 2007). The acupuncture functions in roughly the same way, sending a competitive “bottom-up” signal to the spinal cord.

p201.original: 把疼痛的体验一扫而光不是很好吗？
p201.en: Wouldn't it be nice to wipe out the pain?

p202.original: 尽管这个想法可能很诱人，但事实上这并不好，还有可能是致命的。先天性痛觉不敏感的人感觉不到有什么在伤害他们，他们的身体经常会伤痕累累，他们的四肢会因受伤而变形，如果大脑能够向他们警告危险，这些伤害本可以避免。由于他们没有注意到伤害身体的刺激并做出反应，这些人往往早夭（Manfredi et al.，1981）。一般来说，疼痛是一种重要的防御信号，它警告我们潜在的伤害，帮助我们在恶劣的环境中生存，并提醒我们对疾病和伤害进行治疗。然而，有时慢性疼痛本身似乎是一种疾病，在这种情况下痛觉通路中的神经元变得非常敏感，将正常的感觉刺激放大为疼痛信息（Watkins & Maier，2003）。研究还表明，慢性疼痛可能（至少有时）是由神经损伤组织中的基因通过表观遗传变化“启动”而产生的（Buchheit et al.，2012；Marx，2004）。为了解决这些问题，新的“人工表观遗传”药物正在研发中，这些药物通过模仿人体自身的表观遗传过程来关闭痛觉通路，从而控制慢性疼痛（Chiechio et al.，2010）。
p202.en: Although this idea may be tempting, it is not good in fact, and it may be fatal. People who are insensitive to congenital pains feel nothing to hurt them, their bodies are often scarred, their limbs are deformed by injuries that could have been avoided if the brain had been able to warn them of danger. Because they do not notice and react to the physical irritation, these people tend to die early (Manfredi et al., 1981). In general, pain is an important defensive signal that warns us of potential harm, helps us to survive in a harsh environment and reminds us of the treatment of disease and injury. However, sometimes chronic pain itself appears to be a disease, in which case neurons in the aching road become very sensitive and magnify normal sensory irritation to pain messages (Watkins & Maier, 2003). The study also shows that chronic pain may (at least at times) be caused by the “start” of genes in neuro-damaged tissues through visual genetic changes (Buchheit et al., 2012); Marx, 2004. In order to address these problems, new “artificial genetics” drugs are being developed to control chronic pain by closing the path of pain by imitating the human body's own visual genetic processes (Chiechio et al., 2010).

p204.original: 如果你感到疼痛，你能做什么？
p204.en: What can you do if you feel pain?

p205.original: 从阿司匹林、布洛芬等非处方药到吗啡等处方麻醉药，镇痛药的应用广泛，疗效显著。它们的作用方式多种多样。正如我们所知道的，吗啡通过关闭脊髓门来抑制疼痛信息。阿司匹林则不同，它通过干扰受损组织产生的化学信号来发挥作用（Basbaum & Julius，2006；Carlson，2007）。使用镇痛药的患者应该注意那些副作用，如消化道或肝脏损伤，甚至成瘾。但是研究表明，如果你必须使用麻醉剂来控制剧烈疼痛，那么你上瘾的可能性会远远小于你娱乐性地使用麻醉剂的情况（Melzack，1990）。其原因尚不完全清楚。但对于那些因剧烈疼痛而服用阿片类药物的人来说，阿片类药物可能既不会阻止身体自身产生阿片类物质，也不会产生上瘾者所寻求的快感。
p205.en: From non-prescribed drugs such as aspirin and brofen to prescriptional anaesthesia such as morphine, painkillers are widely used and their efficacy is significant. They function in a variety of ways. As we know, morphine suppresses pain messages by closing the spinal cord. Unlike aspirin, it functions by interfering with chemical signals from damaged tissues (Basbaum & Julius, 2006); Carlson, 2007. Patients who use analgesics should be aware of those side effects, such as digestive tracts or liver damage, and even addiction. However, studies have shown that if you have to use anaesthesia to control severe pain, then you are much less likely to be addicted than you are to be entertained in the use of anaesthetics (Melzack, 1990).
