The reasons for this are not entirely clear. But for those who take opioids for severe pain, opioids may neither prevent the body from producing opioids itself nor create the pleasure sought by addicts.

p206.original: 一个多世纪前，人们开始使用局部麻醉剂。最近（在过去的20年里），对痛觉感受器神经元的研究发现了这些局部麻醉剂中的化学物质是如何发挥其魔力的，科学家们还发现了越来越有前景的镇痛药。我们现在知道，痛觉感受器神经元的“放电”需要钠离子通过细胞膜的通道涌入神经元。局部麻醉剂会阻断这些离子通道，从而抑制疼痛信号，就像堵住地铁车门会阻止乘客进入，最终阻止其到达目的地一样。
p206.en: More than a century ago, local anesthesia was used. Recently (in the last 20 years) studies of the neurons of the pain sensor have found how the chemicals in these local anesthesias have worked, and scientists have found increasingly promising analgesics. We now know that the “discharge” of the pain sensor neurons requires sodium ion to flow into the neurons through the cytological membranes. Local anaesthesia can block these ion channels and thus inhibit pain signals, as if blocking the subway doors would prevent passengers from entering and eventually preventing them from reaching their destination.

p208.original: 人们还可以通过学习心理技巧来控制疼痛，如催眠、放松和分散注意力等程序（Brown，1998）。这些技术如何有效果？它们真的有用吗？
p208.en: People can also control pain by learning psychological skills, such as hypnosis, relaxation and distraction procedures (Brown, 1998). How do these technologies work? Do they really work?

p209.original: 例如，一个在医生办公室接受注射的孩子可能会被要求做一系列深呼吸并把目光移开。你也可能是那些可以用安慰剂来缓解疼痛的人之一，安慰剂是一种假药，但看起来像是真药。例如，安慰剂可以是一种温和的盐水溶液（生理盐水）针剂或糖丸。这类假药通常会在新的镇痛药测试中给对照组使用。当然，它们的有效性与人们相信他们得到了真正的药物有关（Niemi，2009；Wager，2005；Wager et al.，2004）。值得注意的是，大脑对安慰剂和对镇痛药有同样的反应：关闭脊髓门。因为这种安慰剂效应（placebos effect）很常见，任何被认为有效的药物都必须证明自己比安慰剂更强。
p209.en: For example, a child receiving injections in a doctor's office may be required to take a series of deep breaths and look away. And you could be one of those people who can use a placebo to relieve pain, a placebo that's a fake, but looks like a real drug. For example, a placebo can be a mild saline solution (physiosaline) needle or sugar pill. Such counterfeit medicines are usually used by the control group in new painkillers tests. Of course, their effectiveness is linked to the belief that they have access to real drugs (Niemi, 2009); Wager, 2005; Water et al., 2004. It is noteworthy that the brain reacts equally to placebos and painkillers: closing the spinal cord door. Because this placebos effect is common, any drug considered effective must prove itself to be stronger than a placebo.

p210.original: 安慰剂究竟是如何起作用的？显然，对疼痛缓解的期望足以使大脑释放天然“阿片”——止痛内啡肽。我们之所以这样认为，是因为大脑扫描显示，当患者服用安慰剂或镇痛药时，就会激活相同的抑制疼痛的区域（Petrovic et al.，2002）。此外，我们发现对安慰剂有反应的人报告说，当他们服用内啡肽阻断药纳曲酮时，他们的疼痛会加剧（Fields，1978；Fields & Levine，1984）。
p210.en: How does the placebo work? Clearly, the expectation of pain relief is sufficient to free the brain of natural “opioids” — endorphins. We believe this because brain scans show that the same areas of pain inhibition are activated when the patient takes a placebo or painkiller (Petrovic et al., 2002). In addition, those who found reactions to the placebo reported that their pain would increase when they were taking endorphins to block narcoqualone (Filds, 1978); Fields & Levine, 1984.

p211.original: 令人惊奇的是，安慰剂效应并不一定需要安慰剂！在一项对照实验中，法布里奇奥·贝内德蒂（Fabrizio Benedetti）博士和他的同事（Benedetti et al.，2005）发现，即使没有止痛药，医生的临床表现也能抑制疼痛。对心理学家来说，这是一个重要的发现，它表明心理社会环境本身可以产生治疗效果（Guterman，2005）。
p211.en: Surprisingly, the placebo effect does not necessarily require placebo! In a comparative experiment, Dr. Fabrizio Benedetti and his colleague (Benedetti et al., 2005) found that even without painkillers, the doctor's clinical performance could contain pain. For psychologists, this is an important finding, which shows that the psychosocial environment itself can produce therapeutic effects (Guterman, 2005).

p212.original: 用镇痛药控制心理疼痛
p212.en: Use analgesics to control mental pain.

p213.original: 我们都感受过身体上的痛苦，也感受过情感上的痛苦。然而，我们会更认真地对待身体上的痛苦，有时人们会认为自己更容易“克服”情绪上的痛苦。然而，新的研究显示，身体上的痛苦和情感上的痛苦之间有着惊人的联系。在我们的大脑中，这两种体验真的相似吗？
p213.en: We have all experienced physical and emotional pain. However, we will take the physical pain more seriously, and sometimes people will feel that they can more easily “overcome” the emotional pain. However, new research shows an alarming link between physical and emotional suffering. Are these two experiences really similar in our brains?

p214.original: 事实证明，被拒绝的“痛苦”真的很痛苦！心理学家C.内森·德沃尔（C. Nathan DeWall）和他的同事（DeWall et al.，2010）发现对乙酰氨基酚（泰诺中的镇痛成分）可以减轻遭受社会排斥的心理痛苦。与服用安慰剂的志愿者相比，服用对乙酰氨基酚的志愿者在日常生活中的社交排斥感要少得多。在一项后续的实验研究中，首先利用电脑游戏来让玩家感觉到社会排斥，随后的功能磁共振扫描显示，对乙酰氨基酚减少了与社会排斥和身体疼痛相关的大脑区域的活动。除了这些出乎意料的发现之外，这项研究的有趣之处在于发现了生理和心理伤害都涉及大脑中一些相同的疼痛机制。
p214.en: It turns out that the rejected “suffering” is a real pain! The psychologist C. Nathan DeWall and his colleague (DeWall et al., 2010) found that acetaminophenol (the pain-in-the-suffering component of Teno) could alleviate the psychological suffering of social exclusion. The social exclusion of volunteers who take acetaminophenol in their daily lives is much lower than that of volunteers who take placeents. In a follow-up experimental study, computer games were first used to make the player feel socially excluded, and subsequent MRI scans showed that acetaminophenol reduced activity in brain areas associated with social exclusion and physical pain. In addition to these unexpected discoveries, the interesting thing about this study is that physical and psychological injuries are associated with some of the same pain mechanisms in the brain.

p216.original: 疼痛阈限因人而异。有些人总是向牙医要求注射局部麻醉药，而另一些人可能更愿意让牙医不注射麻药就做手术。在实验室里的一项研究发现，与最敏感的被试相比，最不敏感的被试要产生疼痛感需要八倍强度的电击（Rollman & Harris，1987）。另一项实验对疼痛高度敏感的人进行了大脑扫描，结果显示其丘脑和前扣带回皮层的激活程度高于对疼痛耐受性较强的人（Coghill et al.，2003）。这种差异至少有一部分是有遗传基础的（Couzin，2006）。
p216.en: The threshold for pain varies from person to person. Some always ask for local anaesthesia, while others may prefer surgery without anaesthesia. In a laboratory study, it was found that the least sensitive test would require eight times the strength of electroshock to produce pain compared to the most sensitive test (Rollman & Harris, 1987). Another experiment, which scanned the brain of a person with high sensitivity to pain, showed that the cortex and the front button were more active than the more resistant to the pain (Coghill et al., 2003). At least part of the difference is genetic (Couzin, 2006).

p217.original: 我们应该明确这一点：没有证据表明不同种族对疼痛的敏感性存在基因差异，尽管许多报告表明，文化确实影响人们对疼痛的解释和对疼痛刺激的反应。例如，西方妇女经常抱怨分娩是一种极度痛苦的经历，而在某些文化中，妇女在正常分娩时通常几乎没有痛苦的反馈。严重受伤的士兵通常也比受伤的平民需要更少的镇痛药，这可能是因为士兵崇尚“勇敢文化”，或者是因为士兵知道受伤意味着可以离开战区。
p217.en: We should be clear on this point: there is no evidence of genetic differences in the sensitivity of different races to pain, although many reports indicate that culture does influence the interpretation of pain and the response to pain stimulation. Western women, for example, often complain that childbirth is an extremely painful experience, while in some cultures women usually have little or no painful feedback when they give birth normally. Seriously injured soldiers also usually require less painkillers than injured civilians, either because they embrace a “culture of courage” or because they know that injuries mean they can leave the theatre of war.

p218.original: 不过，读者应该注意的是，许多关于疼痛的文化差异的文献更多地依赖于轶事，而不是对照研究。此外，这一领域的科学工作经常会得出相互矛盾的结论（Foster，2006）。也许这项工作产生的最重要的影响之一，就是发现贫困、疼痛和获得医疗保健的机会之间的关系：穷人直至疼痛变得非常严重才会寻求医疗救助。
p218.en: Readers should note, however, that much of the literature on cultural differences in pain relies more on opinio juris than on comparative research. In addition, scientific work in this area often leads to contradictory conclusions (Foster, 2006). Perhaps one of the most important effects of this work is to discover the relationship between poverty, pain and access to health care: the poor do not seek medical assistance until the pain becomes very severe.

p221.original: 疼痛通常预示着在我们身上正在发生一些不愉快和有害的事情。其他哪种感觉也预示着可能的伤害？举一个例子，说明你的另一种感觉是如何发出可能的伤害信号的。
p221.en: Pain usually portends some unpleasant and harmful things that are happening to us. What else does it mean to be a possible injury? Take an example of how your other feeling sends a possible sign of harm.
